q: Under the 1998 ISO Common Policy Conditions, how much written notice must the insurer give the first Named Insured to cancel a commercial policy for nonpayment of premium?
choices: 5 days
10 days
15 days
30 days
explain: The 1998 edition of IL 00 17 requires at least 10 days' notice when the insurer cancels for nonpayment and 30 days for any other reason. State amendatory endorsements can change these periods.

q: The Common Policy Conditions form includes all of the following conditions EXCEPT:
choices: Inspections and Surveys
Examination of Your Books and Records
Transfer of Your Rights and Duties Under This Policy
Vacancy
explain: IL 00 17 has six conditions: Cancellation, Changes, Examination of Books and Records, Inspections and Surveys, Premiums, and Transfer of Rights and Duties. Vacancy is a loss condition in property coverage forms such as CP 00 10.

q: A business buys one policy made up of Common Policy Declarations, Common Policy Conditions, a Commercial Property Coverage Part and a Commercial General Liability Coverage Part. This policy is best described as a:
choices: Commercial package policy
Monoline policy
Businessowners policy
Difference-in-conditions policy
explain: A commercial package policy combines property and liability coverage parts under common declarations and common conditions. A policy with only one coverage part is monoline.
source: IRMI glossary 'commercial package policy'; ISO IL 00 17 11 98 preamble

q: An endorsement, such as Protective Safeguards, that modifies both the Commercial Property and the Farm coverage parts is called a(n):
choices: Interline endorsement
Manuscript endorsement
Coverage part declarations
Broad form endorsement
explain: Interline (IL) forms apply across more than one coverage part. IL 04 15 states that it modifies both the Commercial Property and Farm coverage parts.

q: Supplementary Payments under the 2013 ISO Commercial General Liability (CGL) Coverage Form include up to what amount for bail bonds required because of accidents or traffic law violations arising out of the use of a covered vehicle?
explain: The 2013 ISO CGL pays up to $250 for bail bonds, but the insurer does not have to furnish them. Supplementary payments do not reduce the limits.
source: ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Supplementary Payments 1.b

q: Which statement about Supplementary Payments under the 2013 ISO Commercial General Liability (CGL) Coverage Form is correct?
choices: They reduce the general aggregate limit
They include attorneys' fees taxed against the insured
They apply only under Coverage C – Medical Payments
They are paid in addition to the limits of insurance
explain: The 2013 form says these payments 'will not reduce the limits of insurance.' Court costs are covered, but attorneys' fees taxed against the insured are not. They apply to Coverages A and B.
source: ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Supplementary Payments 1.e, final para.

q: A customer slips in an insured's store and incurs medical bills. Under Coverage C – Medical Payments of the 2013 ISO Commercial General Liability (CGL) Coverage Form, which statement is correct?
choices: Payment requires proof that the insured was negligent
Coverage C pays injured employees of the insured
Expenses must be incurred and reported within one year of the accident
Expenses must be incurred and reported within three years of the accident
explain: Under the 2013 ISO CGL, Coverage C pays regardless of fault, but only for expenses incurred and reported within one year of the accident. Injuries to insureds, which include employees, are excluded.
source: ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Coverage C 1.a(b), 1.b, 2.a

q: The General Aggregate Limit of a Commercial General Liability (CGL) policy applies to all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: Premises and operations damages under Coverage A
Products-completed operations damages under Coverage A
Personal and advertising injury damages under Coverage B
Medical expenses under Coverage C
explain: Products-completed operations BI/PD falls under the separate Products-Completed Operations Aggregate Limit. Everything else counts toward the General Aggregate.
source: ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Sec. III 2-3

q: Which of the following is NOT a personal and advertising injury offense under a Commercial General Liability (CGL) policy?
choices: Malicious prosecution
Wrongful eviction from a room a person occupies
Oral or written publication of material that slanders a person
Bodily injury to a customer caused by a defective product
explain: Bodily injury from a product is Coverage A (BI/PD, products-completed operations), not a Coverage B offense. The other three are listed P&AI offenses.
source: ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Sec. V def. 14

q: During the policy period, the named insured under a 2013 ISO Commercial General Liability (CGL) policy forms a new corporation in which it holds a majority interest. No other similar insurance is available. The new corporation qualifies as a Named Insured:
choices: Only after it is added by endorsement
Until the 30th day after it is formed or the policy period ends, whichever is earlier
Until the 90th day after it is formed or the policy period ends, whichever is earlier
For the rest of the policy period, even if more than 90 days remain
explain: Under the 2013 ISO CGL, newly acquired or formed organizations (other than partnerships, joint ventures or LLCs) are automatic Named Insureds until the 90th day or policy expiration, whichever is earlier. There is no coverage for injury or offenses before the acquisition or formation.
source: ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Sec. II 3

q: An insured business borrows a 22-foot sailboat it does not own and takes clients out on it at no charge. A guest is injured. Under the 2013 ISO Commercial General Liability (CGL) Coverage Form, the aircraft, auto or watercraft exclusion:
choices: Applies
Applies unless the boat was ashore on premises the insured owns or rents
Does not apply only if the clients paid a charge for the trip
Does not apply
explain: Under the 2013 ISO CGL, exclusion g. has an exception for watercraft you do not own that are less than 26 feet long and not carrying persons or property for a charge.
source: ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Excl. g.(2)

q: Which of the following is NOT an insured contract under a Commercial General Liability (CGL) policy?
choices: The part of a premises lease that indemnifies the landlord for fire damage to the rented premises
A sidetrack agreement
An obligation required by ordinance to indemnify a municipality, other than in connection with work for the municipality
An elevator maintenance agreement
explain: A lease of premises is an insured contract, but the part that indemnifies for fire damage to rented premises is specifically carved out. That exposure is handled by the Damage To Premises Rented To You limit.
source: ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Sec. V def. 9.a-e

q: A contractor finishes one part of a project, and the owner starts using that part while other contractors keep working elsewhere on the project. Under a Commercial General Liability policy, an injury arising from the finished part is treated as:
choices: Completed operations
Ongoing operations until all work called for in the contract is finished
Completed operations only after the owner signs a written acceptance certificate
Excluded until the policy renews
explain: Under CG 00 01's "products-completed operations hazard" definition, work is deemed completed at the earliest of: all work called for in the contract is done; all work at the job site is done, if the contract calls for work at more than one site; or that part of the work at a site is put to its intended use by anyone other than another contractor or subcontractor on the same project.
source: ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Sec. V def. 16.a(2)

q: A business has a claims-made CGL policy from January 1, 2026, to January 1, 2027, with a retroactive date of January 1, 2022. It had no earlier claims-made policy, never reported an occurrence to the insurer, and did not buy the Supplemental Extended Reporting Period. Which claim is covered?
choices: Injury on June 1, 2021; claim first made March 1, 2026
Injury on June 1, 2023; claim first made March 1, 2026
Injury on August 1, 2026; claim first made February 1, 2028
Injury on March 1, 2027; claim first made May 1, 2027
explain: Coverage requires injury after the retroactive date and before the policy ends, and a claim first made during the policy period (or an ERP). The 2028 claim is more than 60 days after expiration, and the occurrence was never reported, so even the basic ERP does not apply.
source: FC&S 'Claims-Made CGL Form' (2014, CG 00 02 04 13); Austin & Stanovich, 'The Claims-Made CGL Policy' (2012)

q: Under the Basic Extended Reporting Period of a 2013 ISO claims-made CGL policy, a claim arising from an occurrence reported to the insurer within 60 days after the policy ended may be made up to:
choices: 60 days after the policy ends
1 year after the policy ends
3 years after the policy ends
5 years after the policy ends
explain: Under the 2013 ISO claims-made CGL, the automatic, no-charge basic ERP is 5 years for claims from occurrences reported within 60 days after the policy ends. It is only 60 days for claims from occurrences that were never reported.
source: FC&S 'Claims-Made CGL Form' (2014, CG 00 02 04 13)

q: Under a 2013 ISO claims-made CGL policy, the insured must request the Supplemental Extended Reporting Period in writing within how many days after the policy period ends, and the additional premium cannot exceed what percentage of the annual premium?
choices: Request within 30 days; premium no more than 100%
Request within 60 days; premium no more than 200%
Request within 60 days; premium no more than 300%
Request within 90 days; premium no more than 150%
explain: Under the 2013 ISO claims-made CGL, the supplemental ERP must be requested in writing within 60 days, costs no more than 200% of the annual premium, has unlimited duration, and reinstates the aggregate limits.
source: FC&S 'Claims-Made CGL Form' (2014); Austin & Stanovich (2012)

q: The insurer is not canceling or nonrenewing a 2013 ISO claims-made CGL policy. Within 60 days after the policy period ends, the first Named Insured asks in writing for claim and occurrence information. How soon after the request must the insurer provide it?
choices: Within 10 days
Within 30 days
Within 45 days
Within 90 days
explain: Under the 2013 ISO claims-made CGL, the insurer provides the information within 45 days of the written request. If the insurer cancels or nonrenews, it must provide the information at least 30 days before termination.
source: FC&S 'Claims-Made CGL Form' (2014, CG 00 02 04 13)

q: A building owner requires its contractor to buy an Owners and Contractors Protective (OCP) policy for a project. Which statement about the OCP policy is correct?
choices: The owner is insured for the contractor's operations and its own general supervision of them
Coverage continues after the contractor's work has been completed and put to its intended use
The contractor is the named insured, and the owner is an additional insured
Any return premium is paid to the owner as the first Named Insured
explain: OCP insures the owner (the named insured) for BI/PD arising from the designated contractor's work at the specified location, or from the owner's general supervision. It excludes injury after the work is completed or put to its intended use, and premium refunds go to the 'contractor'.
source: ISO CG 00 09 04 13, Sec. I 1.b(1); Excl. 2.c; Sec. IV 2.e

q: Under the pollution exclusion of the 2013 ISO Commercial General Liability (CGL) Coverage Form, which of the following is still covered?
choices: Cleanup costs ordered by a state environmental agency
Bodily injury from pollutants at a waste disposal site the insured used
Bodily injury from heat, smoke or fumes from a hostile fire at the insured's premises
Property damage from chemicals the insured's subcontractor brought to an outdoor job site and spilled
explain: Under the 2013 ISO CGL, injury from a 'hostile fire' (one that becomes uncontrollable or breaks out from where it was intended to be) is an exception to the premises pollution exclusion. Government-ordered cleanup costs and waste-site and job-site pollutants are excluded.

q: The 1988 ISO Commercial Property Conditions require a legal action against the insurer to be brought within:
choices: 1 year after the loss is reported to the insurer
2 years after the date of the direct physical loss
3 years after the policy period expires
5 years after the date of the direct physical loss
explain: The 1988 CP 00 90 requires full compliance with the coverage part and suit within 2 years after the direct physical loss occurred. Inland marine (CM 00 01) instead runs 2 years from when the insured first has knowledge of the loss.
source: ISO CP 00 90 07 88, D.; CM 00 01 09 04, Gen. Cond. C

q: A building insured by its owner under the 2012 ISO Building and Personal Property Coverage Form has been vacant for 75 consecutive days when a windstorm, a covered cause of loss, damages it. How is the loss handled?
choices: Not covered
Covered in full
Covered, but the payment is reduced by 15%
Covered, but the payment is reduced by 50%
explain: Under the 2012 edition of CP 00 10, after more than 60 consecutive days of vacancy, vandalism, sprinkler leakage (unless the system was protected against freezing), building glass breakage, water damage, theft and attempted theft are not covered. Other covered losses, such as windstorm, are reduced by 15%.

q: A building valued at $500,000 at the time of loss is insured for $300,000 under the 2012 ISO Building and Personal Property Coverage Form with 80% coinsurance and a $1,000 deductible. A $100,000 covered loss occurs. How much does the insurer pay?
explain: Under the 2012 edition of CP 00 10, required insurance is $500,000 × 80% = $400,000. $300,000 ÷ $400,000 = 0.75, and $100,000 × 0.75 = $75,000. Subtract the $1,000 deductible: $74,000.
source: ISO CP 00 10 10 12, F.1 (Coinsurance steps)

sub: Building and Personal Property – Coverage Extensions
q: Which coverage extension in the 2012 ISO Building and Personal Property Coverage Form is correctly matched with its limit?
choices: Newly acquired buildings – $100,000 per building
Personal effects and property of others – $10,000 per premises
Property off-premises – $2,500
Outdoor property – $1,000
explain: In the 2012 edition of CP 00 10, the correct limits are: newly acquired buildings $250,000 (BPP $100,000), property off-premises $10,000, outdoor property $1,000 with $250 per tree, shrub or plant, and personal effects and property of others $2,500.

q: In the 2012 ISO Business Income (and Extra Expense) Coverage Form, the period of restoration for Business Income coverage begins:
choices: Immediately after the direct physical loss
24 hours after the direct physical loss
72 hours after the direct physical loss
When the insured resumes operations
explain: Under the 2012 form, for Business Income the period of restoration starts 72 hours after the direct physical loss. For Extra Expense it starts immediately.

q: A bank has a $100,000 limit and loss payment percentages of 40%–80%–100% under the 2012 ISO Extra Expense Coverage Form. After a fire, its period of restoration is 45 days and it incurs $90,000 of extra expense. The insurer pays:
explain: Under the 2012 form, for a period of restoration of 31–60 days, the second percentage (80%) applies: $100,000 × 80% = $80,000. The remaining $10,000 is not covered.
source: ISO CP 00 50 10 12, C.3 (example)

q: Under the Condominium Commercial Unit-Owners Coverage Form, if the condominium association has other insurance covering the same property, the unit-owner's coverage is:
choices: Excess over the association's insurance
Primary, with the association's insurance as excess
Shared pro rata by limits with the association's insurance
Shared equally with the association's insurance
explain: CP 00 18 is intended to be excess over the association's insurance. The association form (CP 00 17) is intended to be primary and waives subrogation against unit-owners.

q: Unless the insurer specifies otherwise in writing, coverage under the 1995 ISO Builders Risk Coverage Form ends no later than how long after construction is complete?
choices: 30 days
60 days
90 days
1 year
explain: Under the 1995 form, coverage ceases at the earliest of several events, including 90 days after construction is complete or 60 days after the building is occupied in whole or in part or put to its intended use.
source: ISO CP 00 20 06 95, Additional Condition 4.e

q: Which peril is covered by the Causes of Loss – Broad Form but not by the Causes of Loss – Basic Form?
choices: Sprinkler leakage
Sinkhole collapse
Weight of snow, ice or sleet
Theft of business personal property
explain: Broad adds falling objects; weight of snow, ice or sleet; and water damage, plus an Additional Coverage for collapse. Sprinkler leakage and sinkhole collapse are already Basic perils, and theft is not a covered peril in either form.

q: Under the 2017 ISO Causes of Loss – Special Form, the special theft limit for stamps, tickets and letters of credit is:
explain: In the 2017 Special Form, the special theft limits are $2,500 for furs, $2,500 for jewelry and watches, $2,500 for patterns, dies, molds and forms, and $250 for stamps, tickets and letters of credit.

q: Coverage B of the Ordinance or Law Coverage endorsement pays for:
choices: The loss in value of the undamaged portion of the building
The cost to demolish undamaged parts and clear the site
The increased cost to repair or rebuild the building to code
The loss of business income during demolition
explain: Coverage A is loss to the undamaged portion, Coverage B is demolition cost, and Coverage C is increased cost of construction.

q: A toy retailer's inventory roughly doubles from October through December each year. Which commercial property endorsement raises the personal property limit only during scheduled periods?
choices: Spoilage Coverage
Ordinance or Law Coverage
Inflation Guard
Peak Season Limit of Insurance
explain: CP 12 30 increases the limit on covered personal property by a scheduled amount at the described locations, only during the scheduled dates.

q: A store clerk is threatened with a gun and forced to hand over merchandise. Under ISO commercial crime definitions, this is:
choices: Burglary
Forgery
Safe burglary
Robbery
explain: Robbery is the unlawful taking of property from a person's care and custody by someone who caused or threatened bodily harm, or committed an obviously unlawful act witnessed by that person. Burglary involves unlawful entry or exit from premises.
source: ISO CR 00 21 11 15, F. def. 20; IRMI glossary 'burglary'

sub: Commercial Crime – Loss Sustained vs Discovery
q: Under the 2015 ISO Commercial Crime Coverage Form (Loss Sustained Form), loss sustained before cancellation is covered if discovered no later than how long after cancellation, unless replacement insurance takes effect first?
choices: 60 days
90 days
6 months
1 year
explain: Under the 2015 Loss Sustained Form, the extended period to discover loss is one year, but it ends immediately when other replacement insurance takes effect.

sub: Commercial Crime – Loss Sustained vs Discovery
q: Which statement best describes the Commercial Crime Coverage Form (Discovery Form)?
choices: It covers loss discovered during the policy period, no matter when it occurred
It covers only losses that both occur and are discovered during the policy period
It covers occurrences during the policy period discovered up to 1 year after cancellation
It covers only employee theft, not robbery or burglary by outsiders
explain: The discovery form is triggered by discovery, and the occurrence can be at any time. It allows a 60-day period to discover loss after the policy ends. The 1-year tail belongs to the loss sustained form.
source: Rough Notes PF&M 251.4-2 (ISO crime forms analysis); ISO CR 00 21 11 15, E.1.g

q: Under the 2015 ISO Commercial Crime Coverage Form, which loss is covered by the Inside the Premises – Theft of Money and Securities insuring agreement?
choices: Unexplained disappearance of money from the premises
Theft of merchandise from the sales floor by a burglar
Embezzlement of cash from the register by an employee
Counterfeit bills accepted in good faith in a sale
explain: In the 2015 form, this agreement covers money and securities inside the premises (or a financial institution's premises) against theft, disappearance or destruction. Merchandise is 'other property'. Against outside thieves on the premises, it is covered only for robbery of a custodian or safe burglary (Insuring Agreement 4), so ordinary burglary of merchandise from the sales floor is not covered. Employee Theft covers money, securities and other property, so employee embezzlement falls there; counterfeit bills fall under Money Orders and Counterfeit Money.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the classes in the Nationwide Marine Definition?
choices: Commercial property floater risks
Domestic shipments
Personal property floater risks
Buildings and their fixed contents
explain: The classes are imports; exports; domestic shipments; bridges, tunnels and other instrumentalities of transportation and communication; personal property floaters; and commercial property floaters. Buildings and their contents are not marine risks (MCL 500.614 excludes them).
source: IMUA 'Nationwide Marine Definition'; MCL 500.614(4)

q: Under the 2004 ISO Commercial Inland Marine Conditions form, which statement is correct?
choices: The insured may abandon damaged property to the insurer for full payment
Each claim payment reduces the limit of insurance for the remainder of the policy period
Legal action must be brought within 1 year of the loss
Claim payments do not reduce the limit, except for the total loss of a scheduled item
explain: The 2004 edition of CM 00 01 has a Reinstatement of Limit After Loss condition. It also prohibits abandonment and allows legal action within 2 years after the insured first has knowledge of the loss.
source: ISO CM 00 01 09 04, Loss Cond. A, I; Gen. Cond. C

q: Which inland marine class is an ISO filed class rather than a nonfiled class?
choices: Contractors equipment
Accounts receivable
Motor truck cargo
Installation floater
explain: Verisk lists accounts receivable among its filed classes, along with valuable papers, commercial articles, equipment dealers, signs and others. Contractors equipment, motor truck cargo and installation are nonfiled.
source: Verisk 'Commercial Inland Marine' program sheet (2022)

q: A common carrier is generally liable for loss of cargo in its care unless the loss is caused by:
choices: Its driver's negligence
A collision with another vehicle
An act of God
Theft from an unlocked trailer
explain: Common carriers are liable for cargo loss except loss caused by an act of God, the public enemy, an act of the shipper, public authority, or the inherent vice of the goods. The carrier must also prove it was not negligent.
source: Missouri Pacific R.R. v. Elmore & Stahl, 377 U.S. 134 (1964)

q: The Equipment Breakdown Protection Coverage Form values covered property on a replacement cost basis unless:
choices: The insured has fewer than 10 employees
The insured fails to meet a coinsurance requirement
The equipment is more than 20 years old
An Actual Cash Value endorsement is attached
explain: Replacement cost is built into the basic equipment breakdown form. Attaching the Actual Cash Value endorsement (often used for older equipment) changes the valuation to actual cash value.
source: FC&S 'Equipment Breakdown Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016); FC&S 'Equipment Breakdown Endorsements' (2018)

q: In the ISO farm property program, Coverage E applies to:
choices: Dwellings
Scheduled farm personal property
Barns and other farm structures
Loss of use
explain: A = Dwellings, B = Other Private Structures, C = Household Personal Property, D = Loss of Use, E = Scheduled Farm Personal Property, F = Unscheduled Farm Personal Property, G = Other Farm Structures. Edition note: these letters are from FP 00 10 09 94.
source: ISO FP 00 10 09 94; Rough Notes PF&M 471.1

q: In the Farm Liability Coverage Form, Coverage J is:
choices: Bodily Injury and Property Damage Liability
Personal and Advertising Injury Liability
Medical Payments
Employers Liability
explain: Coverage H is BI/PD liability, Coverage I is personal and advertising injury, and Coverage J is medical payments (expenses incurred or ascertained within 3 years of the accident).
source: FC&S 'Farm Liability Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2013)

q: A tenant wants coverage for its legal liability for damage to the landlord's building it occupies, caused by a covered cause of loss. Which commercial property coverage form is designed for this?
choices: Legal Liability Coverage Form
Condominium Commercial Unit-Owners Coverage Form
Builders Risk Coverage Form
Extra Expense Coverage Form
explain: CP 00 40 pays sums the insured is legally obligated to pay for direct physical loss to tangible property of others in its care, custody or control, caused by accident and arising from a covered cause of loss. It includes defense.

q: Under the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form, Business Income covers loss during a period of restoration that occurs within what time after the direct physical loss, and how is it limited?
choices: 6 consecutive months; subject to the building limit
12 consecutive months; not subject to the Section I limits
12 consecutive months; limited to 25% of the Business Personal Property limit
18 consecutive months; subject to a separate declared limit
explain: In the 2013 ISO Businessowners form, Business Income is an Additional Coverage paying actual loss sustained for up to 12 consecutive months, with no dollar limit (it is not subject to the Section I limits). Ordinary payroll is limited to 60 days unless more days are shown.

q: After operations resume, Extended Business Income under the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form lasts until income is restored or up to how many consecutive days, unless the Declarations show more?
explain: In the 2013 ISO Businessowners form, Extended Business Income lasts up to 60 consecutive days after the date property is repaired and operations resume.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I A.5.f(2)

q: A building with a full replacement cost of $400,000 is insured for $240,000 under the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form. A partial loss costs $50,000 to repair; its actual cash value is $30,000. The insured promptly repairs the building. Ignoring the deductible, the insurer pays:
explain: Under the 2013 ISO Businessowners form, the limit is below 80% of replacement cost ($320,000), so the BOP pays the greater of ACV ($30,000) or ($240,000 ÷ $320,000) × $50,000 = $37,500. The BOP has no coinsurance clause, but this 80% rule applies to replacement cost recovery.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I E.5.d(1)(b)

q: Under the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form, the Business Personal Property limit automatically increases by 25%, or by another percentage shown in the Declarations, for seasonal variations, but only if:
choices: The insured reports the values of its business personal property to the insurer by the end of each month
The loss occurs between November 1 and January 31
The insured is a retail store whose stock rises during a peak season shown in the Declarations
The limit is at least 100% of average monthly values for the prior 12 months or time in business, if less
explain: In the 2013 ISO Businessowners form, the seasonal increase applies only if the BPP limit is at least 100% of the average monthly values for the lesser of the preceding 12 months or the time in business.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I C.5

q: Which additional coverage in the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form is correctly matched with its standard limit?
choices: Money Orders and Counterfeit Money – $1,000
Forgery or Alteration – $10,000
Electronic Data – $2,500 per policy year
Fire Extinguisher Systems Recharge Expense – $25,000
explain: The 2013 ISO Businessowners limits are Money Orders and Counterfeit Money $1,000, Forgery or Alteration $2,500, Electronic Data $10,000 per policy year, and Fire Extinguisher Systems Recharge $5,000.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I A.5.j, k, o, p

q: In the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form, the Fire Department Service Charge additional coverage pays up to what amount per premises, unless the Declarations show a different limit?
explain: The 2013 ISO BOP pays up to $2,500 per premises with no deductible. The commercial property BPP form (CP 00 10) pays $1,000.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I A.5.c, D.3

q: Under the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form, the Newly Acquired or Constructed Property extension covers each building up to what limit, and for how many days after acquisition or start of construction, unless values are reported sooner?
choices: Limit $100,000; 60 days
Limit $250,000; 30 days
Limit $250,000; 90 days
Limit $500,000; 90 days
explain: In the 2013 ISO BOP, the extension covers buildings up to $250,000 each and business personal property up to $100,000 per building. Coverage ends at policy expiration, 30 days after acquisition or start of construction, or when values are reported.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I A.6.a

q: Under ISO businessowners program rules, which business is ineligible for a Businessowners policy regardless of its size?
choices: A small apartment building
A neighborhood bar
A three-story office building
A retail clothing store
explain: Ordinary bars and taverns are not an eligible class under ISO's businessowners program, so a neighborhood bar is ineligible at any size. Apartments (any size), offices and retail stores are eligible classes. ISO's 2025 program revision (forms dated August 2024, effective in most states July 1, 2025) added auto service risks, such as repair shops, body shops, car washes and tire dealers, and specialty restaurants such as brew pubs and wine bars, within size and seating limits. Auto dealers remain ineligible. ISO's 2025 overview also lists light manufacturing as eligible, so older lists that exclude all auto repair risks and all manufacturers are out of date.
source: ISO 'Businessowners Policy (BOP) Program' overview (Feb. 11, 2025); IA Magazine 'Multi-State ISO BOP Revision Allows Certain Auto Service Risks' (July 28, 2025); IRMI 'Major Changes to the 2025 ISO Businessowners Program' (Aug. 29, 2025)

q: A Businessowners policy written on the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form shows a Liability and Medical Expenses limit of $1,000,000. The policy's products-completed operations aggregate limit is:
choices: Unlimited
explain: Under the 2013 ISO BOP, both the products-completed operations aggregate and the general aggregate equal twice the Liability and Medical Expenses limit.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. II D.4

q: An accounting firm insured under a Businessowners policy is sued for an error in a client's tax return. Under Section II – Liability, the claim is:
choices: Covered as personal and advertising injury
Covered under Medical Expenses
Covered only if the error appeared in the firm's advertisement
Excluded as a professional service
explain: BP 00 03 excludes injury caused by rendering or failing to render any professional service, including legal and accounting services (and a client's purely financial loss is not bodily injury or property damage in the first place). This exposure needs E&O/professional liability coverage.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. II B.1.j

q: Under Section III – Common Policy Conditions of the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form, the insurer may cancel on as little as 5 days' written notice if:
choices: The building has been vacant or unoccupied 60 or more consecutive days
Premium has not been paid by the due date
The insured has filed two or more claims within the same policy year
The insured changes agents or moves its business to a new location
explain: In the 2013 ISO BOP, the 5-day cancellation applies to listed building conditions such as 60+ consecutive days of vacancy or unoccupancy (other than seasonal unoccupancy or construction, renovation or addition), repairs not started within 30 days of loss payment, or a vacate or demolition order. Nonpayment requires 10 days, and other reasons 30 days. For a policy issued in Michigan, however, state law requires the insurer to mail its cancellation notice at least 10 days before cancellation, for both fire and casualty insurance.

q: In the Protective Safeguards endorsement schedule, the symbol 'P-1' refers to:
choices: Automatic fire alarm
Security service with hourly rounds
Automatic sprinkler system
Service contract with a privately owned fire department
explain: In the 2013 Businessowners Protective Safeguards endorsement (BP 04 30 07 13), P-1 is an automatic sprinkler system, P-2 an automatic fire alarm, P-3 a security service, P-4 a service contract with a privately owned fire department, P-5 an automatic commercial cooking exhaust and extinguishing system, and P-9 a system described in the schedule. The commercial property version (CP 04 11 10 12) also has P-5; the older interline version (IL 04 15 04 98) lists only P-1 through P-4 and P-9.

q: A Businessowners policy includes the Protective Safeguards endorsement, which lists an automatic fire alarm connected to a central station. The insured knows the alarm has been disconnected for weeks but does not tell the insurer. A fire then damages the building. The fire loss is:
choices: Covered in full
Covered, subject to a 15% reduction
Covered for business personal property only
Excluded
explain: The endorsement excludes fire loss if, before the fire, the insured knew of a suspension or impairment of a listed safeguard and failed to notify the insurer, or failed to keep it in complete working order.

q: A restaurant loses income when a fire at an off-premises power substation interrupts its electric service. Which Businessowners policy endorsement covers the lost income?
choices: Utility Services – Time Element
Utility Services – Direct Damage
Spoilage Coverage
Protective Safeguards
explain: Utility Services – Time Element (BP 04 57) covers Business Income and Extra Expense from interruption of utility service caused by covered damage to scheduled off-premises utility property. Direct Damage (BP 04 56) covers physical damage to covered property.

q: Under the Utility Services endorsements for a Businessowners policy, loss caused by damage to overhead transmission lines is:
choices: Covered whenever power supply property is indicated in the Schedule
Not covered under either endorsement
Covered only if indicated in the Schedule
Covered only for water supply property
explain: Communication and power supply property do not include overhead transmission lines unless the Schedule indicates them.

sub: Selected Endorsements – Hired and Non-Owned Auto
q: An employee runs a business errand in her own car and causes an accident. The employer is sued. Which Businessowners policy endorsement or optional coverage covers the employer's liability?
choices: Hired Auto and Non-Owned Auto Liability
Utility Services – Time Element
Protective Safeguards
Employee Dishonesty optional coverage
explain: BP 04 04 covers BI/PD from use of a non-owned auto in the insured's business by any person, and from use of hired autos. A premium must be shown in the Declarations.
source: FC&S 'Businessowners Program Endorsements Described' (2020, BP 04 04 01 10)

q: When claims exhaust the aggregate limit of an underlying liability policy, an umbrella policy with a drop-down provision will:
choices: Suspend coverage until the underlying policy renews
Respond in place of the exhausted underlying coverage
Pay only defense costs
Require the insured to buy a new underlying limit first
explain: One umbrella function is to drop down and pick up where the underlying policy leaves off when its aggregate is exhausted. Umbrellas also provide excess limits and cover some claims not covered by underlying policies, subject to a self-insured retention.
source: IRMI glossary 'umbrella liability policy'; 'drop down provision'

q: Under a directors and officers (D&O) liability policy, which insuring agreement reimburses the corporation for amounts it pays to indemnify its directors and officers?
choices: Side A
Side B
Side C
Side D
explain: Side A covers directors and officers directly when the company can't or won't indemnify. Side B (corporate reimbursement) reimburses the company. Side C (entity coverage) covers the organization itself, typically for securities claims.
source: IRMI glossary 'Side A coverage', 'corporate reimbursement coverage', 'entity securities coverage'

q: The trustee of a company's 401(k) plan makes an imprudent investment choice. Plan participants sue for breach of fiduciary duty under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA). Which coverage is designed to respond?
choices: ERISA fidelity bond
Commercial crime employee theft coverage
Employment practices liability
Fiduciary liability insurance
explain: Fiduciary liability covers errors in administering benefit plans under ERISA. The ERISA fidelity bond protects the plan only against fraud or dishonesty by people handling plan funds.
source: IRMI glossary 'fiduciary liability'; 29 U.S.C. 1112(a)

q: A former employee sues her employer alleging wrongful termination and sexual harassment. Which coverage is designed for this claim?
choices: Employment practices liability insurance
Workers' compensation insurance
CGL Coverage A – Bodily Injury and Property Damage Liability
Fiduciary liability insurance
explain: EPLI covers wrongful acts arising from the employment process (e.g., wrongful termination, harassment, discrimination). Workers compensation covers job-related injury and disease, and CGL Coverage A excludes bodily injury to employees.
source: IRMI glossary 'employment practices liability insurance'

q: Michigan law requires a retail liquor licensee to file proof of financial responsibility for dram shop liability of not less than:
explain: The proof may be liquor liability insurance, a surety bond, cash or securities, or a group self-insurance pool. A licensee may cancel liquor liability insurance only on 30 days' notice to the commission, with replacement proof.

q: In a construction performance bond, the project owner who is protected if the contractor fails to perform is the:
choices: Principal
Surety
Obligee
Indemnitor
explain: The bond is executed by the principal (the contractor) and the surety to assure the principal's obligations to a third party, the obligee.
source: FAR 48 CFR 28.001 'Bond'

q: Which bond assures that a contractor will pay the persons who supply labor and material for the project?
choices: Bid bond
Performance bond
License and permit bond
Payment bond
explain: A payment bond assures payment to suppliers of labor and material. A performance bond secures completion of the contract. A bid bond assures the bidder will sign the contract and furnish the required bonds.
source: FAR 48 CFR 28.001

q: How does a surety bond differ from a typical insurance policy?
choices: The surety expects losses and prices the bond to pay them
The obligee pays the premium and indemnifies the surety
Only two parties are involved: the surety and the principal
The principal must reimburse the surety for losses it pays
explain: A surety bond is a three-party contract. The surety is secondarily liable and underwrites expecting no losses, and the principal must indemnify the surety for any loss it pays.
source: surety.org 'What is a Surety Bond?'; SFAA/AGC Surety Claims Guide

q: Under Michigan's surplus lines law, each surplus lines policy delivered to an insured must bear a notice, in red ink and at least 10-point type, stating that:
choices: The policy is protected by the Michigan Property and Casualty Guaranty Association if the insurer becomes insolvent and cannot pay claims
The insurer is not licensed by Michigan, and if it is insolvent, payment of claims may not be guaranteed
The rates and forms were approved by DIFS before the policy was issued
The agent is personally liable for claims if the insurer becomes insolvent
explain: MCL 500.1922 requires the notice: 'This insurance has been placed with an insurer that is not licensed by the state of Michigan. In case of insolvency, payment of claims may not be guaranteed.'

q: Under Michigan's surplus lines law, a surplus lines licensee must pay what tax and fee on surplus lines premiums written?
choices: 1% premium tax and 0.5% regulatory fee
2% premium tax and 0.5% regulatory fee
2% premium tax and 1% regulatory fee
3% premium tax and no regulatory fee
explain: The licensee files sworn statements by February 15 and August 15 and pays the 2% premium tax plus a 0.5% regulatory fee.

q: Under Michigan's surplus lines law, coverage is presumed to be available from authorized insurers for all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: Private passenger auto physical damage
Any coverage readily available from 3 or more authorized insurers at competitive terms
Michigan no-fault auto insurance for someone who is not a self-insurer
Coverage not obtainable after a diligent search among authorized insurers
explain: Coverage that cannot be procured after a diligent search among authorized insurers is presumed UNAVAILABLE and may be exported. The other three are presumed available.

q: Which statement about the Write Your Own (WYO) program of the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) is correct?
choices: Private insurers write and service policies in their own names; the federal government pays losses
Policies are sold and serviced by FEMA employees instead of private insurers
WYO companies set their own flood rates and policy forms, subject to state insurance department approval
WYO policies provide broader coverage than the same policy bought from NFIP Direct
explain: WYO companies are private P&C insurers that write and service NFIP policies in their own names, and the federal government pays all losses. Coverage is the same whether the policy comes from a WYO company or NFIP Direct.
source: FEMA brochure 'Meeting the Flood Insurance Requirement' (07-2024); agents.floodsmart.gov 'Flood Insurance 101'

q: A homeowner buys a National Flood Insurance Program flood policy at the closing of a new mortgage loan. What waiting period applies?
choices: None
1 day
15 days
30 days
explain: The standard waiting period is 30 days, but there is none when coverage is bought in connection with making, increasing, extending or renewing a loan. Other exceptions apply after map revisions and for post-wildfire flooding.
source: agents.floodsmart.gov 'Flood Insurance 101' (accessed Oct 2026)

q: What is the maximum building coverage available from the National Flood Insurance Program for a non-residential building?
explain: Non-residential maximums are $500,000 building and $500,000 contents. Single-family and 2-4 family residential buildings max out at $250,000 (residential contents $100,000); other residential buildings with 5 or more units can be insured up to $500,000.
source: 44 CFR 61.6(a); FEMA 'NFIP Summary of Coverage - Commercial Property' (01-2024)

q: Under the National Flood Insurance Program's Risk Rating 2.0 rules, what is the minimum building deductible for a residential building with more than $100,000 of building coverage and no pre-FIRM statutory discount?
explain: The minimum is $1,000 for building coverage of $100,000 or less and $1,250 for over $100,000. Pre-FIRM statutorily discounted buildings have $1,500/$2,000 minimums. Values as stated in FEMA guidance current in 2024–2025.
source: FEMA RR2.0 'Simple Guide for Residential Manufactured/Mobile Homes' (citing FIM Sec. 3)

q: Which statement about a risk retention group under the federal Liability Risk Retention Act is correct?
choices: It may write property and liability insurance for the general public
It must be licensed as an insurer in every state where it does business
It must participate in each state's insurance guaranty association
It is owned by its members and writes only liability insurance for them
explain: An RRG is chartered as a liability insurer in one state, owned by members in similar businesses, and limited to liability coverage. States may not require or permit it to join guaranty funds.

q: Which one of the following is a third-party cyber coverage?
choices: Forensic investigation costs
Payments to consumers whose data was exposed
Customer notification and call-center costs
Business income lost during a network outage
explain: Third-party coverage protects the insured from liability claims by others, such as affected consumers. Forensics, notification and business interruption are first-party costs.
source: NAIC 'Cyber Insurance' consumer guide

q: Which cause of loss is excluded under Section I – Property of the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form?
choices: Fire
Flood
Hail
Lightning
explain: Section I of the 2013 ISO Businessowners form covers direct physical loss unless the loss is excluded. Its Water exclusion removes flood, surface water, waves, tides and overflow of any body of water, whether or not driven by wind. Fire, hail and lightning are covered and are also 'specified causes of loss'; flood needs a separate flood policy or the Flood Coverage endorsement.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I A.3, B.1.g(1), H.12; ISO 'Businessowners Policy (BOP) Program' overview (Feb. 11, 2025), p. 15 (Flood Coverage endorsement)

q: With no optional coverages or endorsements, which loss is covered under Section I – Property of the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form?
choices: An employee steals merchandise from the stockroom
A con artist tricks a clerk into handing over merchandise
Stock is missing, shown only by an inventory shortage
An employee smashes the store's display cases in anger
explain: The 2013 form's Dishonesty exclusion does not apply to acts of destruction by employees, so vandalism by an employee is covered. Theft by employees is excluded unless the Employee Dishonesty optional coverage applies. The False Pretense exclusion removes property handed over because of a trick, and the form does not pay for property missing when the only evidence is an inventory shortage.

q: Section I – Property of the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form excludes continuous or repeated seepage or leakage of water that occurs over a period of:
choices: 3 days or more
7 days or more
14 days or more
30 days or more
explain: The 2013 ISO Businessowners form excludes continuous or repeated seepage or leakage of water, or the presence or condensation of humidity, moisture or vapor, that occurs over a period of 14 days or more.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I B.2.p

q: In the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form, no deductible applies to which of the following coverages?
choices: Business Income
Forgery or Alteration
Money and Securities
Outdoor Signs
explain: The 2013 form applies no deductible to Fire Department Service Charge, Business Income, Extra Expense, Civil Authority and Fire Extinguisher Systems Recharge Expense. Forgery or Alteration, Money and Securities, Outdoor Signs and Employee Dishonesty are subject to the Optional Coverage Deductible shown in the Declarations. Business Income still begins only 72 hours after the loss, under the 'period of restoration' definition.

q: According to ISO's 2025 businessowners program overview, the base property deductible in the ISO Businessowners policy is:
explain: ISO's February 2025 program overview states that the base property deductible in the ISO BOP is $500. Optional fixed deductibles of $250, $1,000, $2,500, $5,000, $7,500 and $10,000 are available, as are 1%, 2% and 5% windstorm or hail deductibles. The 2013 coverage form itself states no amount; it applies the deductible shown in the Declarations.
source: ISO 'Businessowners Policy (BOP) Program' overview (Feb. 11, 2025), p. 6; ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I D.1

q: A business insures two locations under one policy written on the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form. It breaches a policy condition at Location A. A covered fire then damages Location B, where no breach exists. The fire loss at Location B is:
choices: Covered
Not covered
Covered only after the breach at Location A is corrected
Covered, but reduced by 15%
explain: Under the Control of Property condition of the 2013 form, a breach of a condition at one location does not affect coverage at any location where no breach exists at the time of loss. The same condition says an act or neglect of anyone beyond the insured's direction or control does not affect the insurance. The 15% reduction comes from the Vacancy loss condition, which does not apply here.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I F.1, E.8

q: A bank is shown in the Declarations as mortgageholder on a building insured under the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form. The bank has started foreclosure when a covered fire damages the building. The bank:
choices: Loses its right to loss payment
May collect only after the foreclosure is completed
Still has the right to receive loss payment
May collect only the premium it has paid
explain: The Mortgageholders condition of the 2013 form gives the mortgageholder the right to receive loss payment even if it has started foreclosure or similar action. Covered building losses are paid to each mortgageholder shown in the Declarations, in order of precedence, as interests may appear.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I F.2.b-c

q: Under the Employee Dishonesty optional coverage of the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form, a loss sustained during the policy period is covered only if it is discovered no later than how long after the policy period ends?
choices: 60 days
6 months
1 year
3 years
explain: The 2013 form pays only for covered loss sustained during the policy period and discovered no later than one year from the end of the policy period. The coverage is cancelled as to an employee as soon as the insured, or a partner, member, manager, officer or director not in collusion, discovers a dishonest act by that employee.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I G.3.f-g

q: A robber takes a store's cash receipts from its manager while she is carrying them to the bank. Which coverage in the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form is designed to cover this loss?
choices: Business Personal Property coverage
Employee Dishonesty optional coverage
Personal Property Off-premises coverage extension
Money and Securities optional coverage
explain: The Money and Securities optional coverage pays for theft, disappearance or destruction of money and securities at the premises, at a bank, in certain living quarters, or in transit between those places. Money and securities are not Covered Property under Business Personal Property; the Personal Property Off-premises extension excludes them; and Employee Dishonesty covers only dishonest acts of employees.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I A.2.b, A.6.b, G.2.a, G.3.a

q: Which of the following is one of the 'specified causes of loss' defined in the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form?
choices: Earthquake
Mine subsidence
Mudslide or mudflow
Sinkhole collapse
explain: The 2013 form lists fire; lightning; explosion; windstorm or hail; smoke; aircraft or vehicles; riot or civil commotion; vandalism; leakage from fire extinguishing equipment; sinkhole collapse; volcanic action; falling objects; weight of snow, ice or sleet; and water damage. Earthquake and mine subsidence fall under the Earth Movement exclusion, and mudslide or mudflow falls under the Water exclusion.

q: In the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form, which item meets the definition of 'money' rather than 'securities'?
choices: Revenue stamps in current use
Tokens and tickets in current use
Traveler's checks held for sale
Unused value in a postage meter
explain: In the 2013 form, 'money' means currency, coins and bank notes in current use with a face value, plus traveler's checks, register checks and money orders held for sale to the public. 'Securities' include tokens, tickets, revenue and other stamps in current use, and unused value in a meter.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I H.7, H.11

q: Section II – Liability of the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form contains which two coverages?
choices: Business Liability and Medical Expenses
Business Liability and Employers Liability
Business Liability and Liquor Liability
Medical Expenses and Hired Auto Liability
explain: Section II of the 2013 form has two coverages. Business Liability covers bodily injury, property damage and personal and advertising injury in one insuring agreement with a duty to defend. Medical Expenses pays for bodily injury caused by an accident, regardless of fault. Employers liability is excluded, liquor liability is excluded for insureds in the business of manufacturing, distributing, selling, serving or furnishing alcohol, and hired and non-owned auto liability is added by endorsement.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. II A.1-2, B.1.c, B.1.e; ISO 'Businessowners Policy (BOP) Program' overview (Feb. 11, 2025), p. 9 (Hired Auto And Non-owned Auto Liability endorsement)

q: A customer slips and falls in an insured's store on September 15, 2025. The store's 2013 ISO Businessowners policy ran from January 1, 2025, to January 1, 2026. The insured first learns of the fall when sued in April 2026 and notifies the insurer at once. The claim is:
choices: Not covered
Covered
Covered only if an extended reporting period was purchased
Covered only if the policy had been renewed
explain: Business Liability in the 2013 form covers bodily injury caused by an occurrence in the coverage territory that occurs during the policy period, provided no listed insured knew of it before the policy period. The date the suit is filed does not matter. Extended reporting periods belong to claims-made forms, and this coverage is occurrence-based.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. II A.1.b(1), E.2

sub: Section II - Liability > Who is an Insured
q: A corporation is the named insured under a Businessowners policy written on the 2013 ISO form. Its stockholders are insureds:
choices: For all of their business and personal activities
Only with respect to their liability as stockholders
Only while acting as executive officers
Only if each stockholder is named in the Declarations
explain: When the named insured is an organization other than a partnership, joint venture or LLC, the 2013 form makes the organization an insured. Its executive officers and directors are insureds only for their duties as officers or directors, and its stockholders are insureds only with respect to their liability as stockholders.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. II C.1.d

sub: Section II - Liability > Who is an Insured
q: Dan owns a hardware store as a sole proprietor and is the named insured under a Businessowners policy written on the 2013 ISO form. Which person is also an insured with respect to the conduct of the store's business?
choices: A customer shopping in the store
An independent contractor hired to fix the roof
Dan's landlord
Dan's spouse
explain: When the named insured is an individual, the 2013 form makes the individual and his or her spouse insureds, but only for the conduct of a business the individual solely owns. Employees and volunteer workers are also insureds for business duties. Customers, independent contractors and landlords are not; a landlord can be added by an additional insured endorsement.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. II C.1.a, C.2.a; ISO 'Businessowners Policy (BOP) Program' overview (Feb. 11, 2025), p. 8 (Additional Insured – Managers Or Lessors Of Premises)

q: Under the liability conditions of the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form, an insured who voluntarily makes a payment or incurs an expense without the insurer's consent does so at its own cost, except for:
choices: First aid
Medical bills up to the Medical Expenses limit
Repairs to a customer's damaged property
Settlements of less than $1,000
explain: The 2013 form's Duties condition says no insured will, except at its own cost, voluntarily make a payment, assume any obligation or incur any expense, other than for first aid, without the insurer's consent. The insured must also notify the insurer as soon as practicable of an occurrence or offense that may result in a claim.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. II E.2.a, E.2.d

q: A customer is injured at an insured's store during the policy period, and the insured later goes bankrupt. Under the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form, the insurer:
choices: Is relieved of its obligations under the policy
Remains bound by its obligations under the policy
Owes defense costs but not damages
Owes damages only up to the Medical Expenses limit
explain: The Bankruptcy condition of the 2013 form says bankruptcy or insolvency of the insured or the insured's estate will not relieve the insurer of its obligations. Michigan law requires liability policies to contain a provision to the same effect.

q: Under the liability definitions of the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form, a forklift used only in the insured's warehouse, and not subject to any motor vehicle registration or insurance law, is classified as:
choices: An auto
Impaired property
Mobile equipment
Your product
explain: In the 2013 form, 'mobile equipment' includes bulldozers, farm machinery, forklifts and other vehicles designed for use principally off public roads, unless the vehicle is subject to a compulsory or financial responsibility law or other motor vehicle insurance or registration law. The aircraft, auto or watercraft exclusion does not apply to mobile equipment. Its own exclusion applies only to transportation of mobile equipment by an auto owned or operated by, or rented or loaned to, an insured, and to use in prearranged racing, speed, demolition or stunting activity.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. II F.2, F.12, B.1.g-h

q: In Section II – Liability of the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form, the definition of 'property damage' treats electronic data as:
choices: Not tangible property
Tangible property
Tangible property only if the device storing it is physically damaged
Tangible property only if it belongs to someone other than the insured
explain: The 2013 form defines 'property damage' as physical injury to tangible property, including resulting loss of use, or loss of use of tangible property that is not physically injured. It then states that, for the purposes of this insurance, electronic data is not tangible property, with no exception for data on a damaged device or data owned by others. A separate Electronic Data exclusion removes damages for loss of, loss of use of, damage to, or corruption of electronic data, except liability for bodily injury.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. II F.17, B.1.q

q: Which loss is part of the premises and operations exposure, rather than the products-completed operations hazard, under the 2013 ISO Commercial General Liability (CGL) Coverage Form?
choices: A toaster bought at the insured's store last month shorts out and burns a customer at home
A railing the insured contractor finished installing last year breaks and injures a guest
A water heater the insured plumber finished installing last month leaks and floods a basement
A board the insured's crew drops while still framing a house hits a passerby
explain: The products-completed operations hazard covers injury or damage away from premises the insured owns or rents that arises out of the insured's product or work, but not work that has not yet been completed or abandoned. Injury from work still in progress is therefore a premises and operations exposure; the toaster is a product away from the premises, and the railing and water heater are completed work.
source: ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Sec. V def. 16.a (products-completed operations hazard); IRMI glossary "premises-operations" (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13)

q: A manufacturer's CGL policy includes the 1985 ISO Pollution Liability Coverage Extension endorsement. Which loss is still excluded?
choices: Bodily injury to neighbors from fumes accidentally released at the insured's plant
Property damage to a farmer's crops from an accidental chemical spill at the insured's plant
Cost of cleaning up pollutants that a state environmental agency orders the insured to remove
Bodily injury to a homeowner from fumes released at a job site where the insured's crew is working
explain: The endorsement states that paragraph (1) of the CGL pollution exclusion does not apply, so bodily injury and property damage from pollutants are covered like other occurrences. Paragraph (2) still applies: it excludes costs of testing for, cleaning up or otherwise responding to pollutants because of a request, order or regulatory requirement, or a governmental suit for such costs.
source: ISO CG 04 22 11 85 (entire text: "Paragraph (1.) of Exclusion f. of COVERAGE A (Section I) does not apply"; copy at iiat.org InfoCentral); ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Excl. f.(1)-(2); Rough Notes PF&M 270.6-3 "Pollution Exclusion and Limited Coverage" (CG 04 22 "does not cover cleanup costs")

q: In the 2012 ISO Condominium Association Coverage Form, fixtures and appliances inside individual units are covered as Building property when:
choices: The association agreement requires the association to insure them
The unit-owner has bought no insurance of his or her own on them
The unit is rented to a tenant who uses them in a business
The unit-owner pays the association a special assessment for them
explain: Building includes fixtures, improvements and alterations that are part of the building, and appliances, inside a unit, regardless of ownership, if the Condominium Association Agreement requires the association to insure them. Otherwise, personal property owned by, used by or in the care of a unit-owner is not Building property.
source: ISO CP 00 17 10 12, A.1.a.(6) and the closing paragraph of A.1.a

q: A unit-owner negligently starts a fire that damages the condominium building. The association's insurer pays the loss under the 2012 ISO Condominium Association Coverage Form. Which statement about the insurer's right to recover its payment from the unit-owner is correct?
choices: It may recover its full payment from the unit-owner
It may recover from the unit-owner only if the association agrees
It may recover from the unit-owner only the cost to repair that owner's unit
It may not recover its payment from the unit-owner
explain: Under the Waiver of Rights of Recovery condition of the Condominium Association Coverage Form, the insurer waives its rights to recover payment from any unit-owner of the condominium shown in the Declarations, so it cannot subrogate against the negligent unit-owner.
source: ISO CP 00 17 10 12, E.9 (Waiver Of Rights Of Recovery)

q: A restaurant's 2007 ISO Spoilage Coverage endorsement covers Power Outage. Which loss of refrigerated food is covered?
choices: An employee unplugs the walk-in cooler to clean it and forgets to plug it back in
The utility cannot supply enough power because of a fuel shortage
A storm knocks down utility lines a mile away, cutting power to the restaurant
The restaurant's own generator lacks the capacity to meet demand during a heat wave
explain: Power Outage covers spoilage from a complete or partial interruption of electrical power, on or off the premises, due to conditions beyond the insured's control. The endorsement excludes disconnecting refrigeration from its power source, a utility's inability to supply enough power because of lack of fuel or governmental order, and a premises power source's lack of generating capacity to meet demand.

q: A 2007 ISO Spoilage Coverage endorsement covers Breakdown or Contamination and shows that a refrigeration maintenance agreement applies. If the insured voluntarily ends the agreement without telling the insurer, the spoilage coverage is:
choices: Automatically suspended at the involved location
Canceled after 10 days' written notice to the insured
Continued until the next policy anniversary
Reduced by 15% until a new agreement is signed
explain: When Breakdown or Contamination is designated and a refrigeration maintenance agreement is shown as applicable, the insured must maintain a refrigeration maintenance or service agreement. If the insured voluntarily terminates it and does not notify the insurer, the endorsement's coverage is automatically suspended at the involved location.
source: ISO CP 04 40 06 07, H. (Refrigeration Maintenance Agreements)

q: The commercial property Value Reporting Form is best suited to a business whose:
choices: Property values stay level throughout the year
Building has been vacant for more than 60 days
Business income depends on a single supplier
Inventory values rise and fall during the year
explain: Reporting form coverage lets an insured with fluctuating inventory values carry a limit high enough for its peak values while paying premium on the values actually reported. Under the 2002 ISO form, the premium charged at inception is an advance premium, adjusted after the policy year based on the average of the insured's reports of value.
source: IRMI glossary "reporting form coverage" (synonym: value reporting form) (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13); ISO CP 13 10 04 02, C.1-2

q: Under the 2002 ISO Value Reporting Form, if a loss occurs before the insured has filed the first required report of values, the insurer pays no more than what percentage of the amount it would otherwise have paid?
explain: If the first required report of values has not been submitted at the time of loss, the insurer pays no more than 75% of what it would otherwise have paid, and only for loss at locations shown in the Declarations. If a later required report is missing, it pays no more than the values last reported for the location.
source: ISO CP 13 10 04 02, B.4 (Failure To Submit Reports)

q: Under the 2002 ISO Value Reporting Form, the last report before a loss showed $150,000 of property at a location actually worth $200,000 on the report dates. The limit is $300,000, the loss $40,000 and the deductible $500. What will the insurer pay?
explain: The Full Reporting condition replaces coinsurance: the insurer pays no greater proportion of the loss than the values reported divided by the actual values on the report dates. $150,000 / $200,000 = 0.75; 0.75 x $40,000 = $30,000; minus the $500 deductible = $29,500.
source: ISO CP 13 10 04 02, B.2 (Full Reporting) and its Example of Under Reporting

q: A thief hides in a store until closing, takes merchandise, and forces open a rear door to get out. In insurance terms, this loss is best described as:
choices: Robbery
Burglary
Safe burglary
Vandalism
explain: Burglary is theft of property from within premises by a person who unlawfully enters or exits (breaks out of) the premises; the National Alliance definition adds that the entry or exit be evidenced by marks of forcible entry or exit, such as the forced rear door. No one was threatened (robbery), and no safe was opened (safe burglary).
source: IRMI glossary "burglary" (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13); National Alliance Research Academy glossary "burglary" (riskeducation.org, retrieved 2026-10-13)

q: In insurance terms, which element must be present for a theft to be a burglary?
choices: A person on the premises was threatened with bodily harm
Property was taken from inside a locked safe or vault
The thief entered or left the premises unlawfully
The thief was an employee of the insured
explain: Burglary requires unlawful entry into or exit from the premises, and the National Alliance definition also requires marks of forcible entry or exit. Robbery, by contrast, is a taking from a person by one who causes or threatens bodily harm or commits an obviously unlawful act that person witnesses.
source: IRMI glossary "burglary" (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13); National Alliance Research Academy glossary "burglary" (riskeducation.org, retrieved 2026-10-13); ISO CR 00 21 11 15, F.20 (robbery)

q: The 2015 ISO Commercial Crime Coverage Form defines theft as:
choices: The unlawful taking of property to the deprivation of the insured
The unlawful taking of property from a person who is threatened with bodily harm
The unlawful taking of property from inside a locked safe or vault
The unlawful taking of property by a person who forcibly enters the premises
explain: Theft is the broadest crime term in the form: any unlawful taking of property to the deprivation of the insured. The other choices describe the narrower terms robbery, safe burglary and burglary.

q: A business learns that its bookkeeper stole from a former employer before being hired. Under the 2015 ISO Commercial Crime Coverage Form, Employee Theft coverage for the bookkeeper:
choices: Continues until the policy expires
Ends at the next policy anniversary
Ends 30 days after the business gives the insurer written notice
Ends as soon as the business learns of the theft
explain: Employee Theft terminates as to any employee as soon as the insured, or a partner, member, manager, officer, director or trustee not in collusion with the employee, learns of theft or any other dishonest act by that employee, whether committed before or after the employee was hired. The insurer can also end it for an employee by a notice that takes effect at least 30 days after mailing.
source: ISO CR 00 21 11 15, E.2.a (Termination As To Any Employee)

q: For Employee Theft coverage under the 2015 ISO Commercial Crime Coverage Form, which person is NOT an employee?
choices: A worker leased to the insured by a labor leasing firm under a written agreement
A temporary worker filling in for an employee who is on leave
An independent contractor hired to install the insured's new computer system
A former employee, during the first 30 days after being laid off
explain: Employee includes a person in the insured's service and for the first 30 days after termination (unless terminated for theft or dishonesty), a temporary worker substituting for an employee on leave or meeting seasonal or short-term needs, and a worker leased under a written agreement with a labor leasing firm. It does not include an independent contractor.

q: Which loss is covered by the Forgery or Alteration insuring agreement of the 2015 ISO Commercial Crime Coverage Form?
choices: A customer's check payable to the insured is returned for insufficient funds
A thief forges the insured's signature on a check drawn on the insured's account
The insured accepts a counterfeit $100 bill from a customer in exchange for merchandise
A burglar takes cash from the insured's locked cash drawer overnight
explain: Forgery or Alteration covers loss from forgery or alteration of checks, drafts, promissory notes or similar written promises, orders or directions to pay a sum certain in money that are made or drawn by or drawn upon the insured (or its agent). Counterfeit money is covered under Money Orders and Counterfeit Money, and a bad check that was not forged or altered is not covered.

q: A business insured under the 2015 ISO Commercial Crime Coverage Form is sued for refusing to pay a check drawn on its account on the basis that it was forged. The insurer consents in writing to the defense. The insured's reasonable legal expenses are paid:
choices: Only if the insured wins the suit
Only after the deductible is met
Within the Limit of Insurance, which they reduce
In addition to the Limit of Insurance
explain: If the insured is sued for refusing to pay a covered instrument on the basis that it was forged or altered, and has the insurer's written consent to defend, the insurer pays reasonable legal expenses in addition to the Limit of Insurance. The deductible does not apply to these legal expenses.

sub: Crime Coverages > Inside the Premises - Robbery or Safe Burglary of Other Property
q: Which loss is covered by Inside the Premises – Robbery or Safe Burglary of Other Property in the 2015 ISO Commercial Crime Coverage Form?
choices: Cash taken from the register by a robber who threatens the cashier
Merchandise a burglar takes from store shelves after breaking in overnight
Merchandise taken at gunpoint from a clerk inside the store
Merchandise taken at gunpoint from an employee making deliveries
explain: This insuring agreement covers other property (property other than money and securities) inside the premises against actual or attempted robbery of a custodian, such as an employee caring for property inside the premises, or actual or attempted safe burglary. Money is covered under Inside the Premises – Theft of Money and Securities, property in a messenger's care under Outside the Premises, and theft from open shelves is not covered by this insuring agreement.
source: ISO CR 00 21 11 15, A.3, A.4, A.5; F.4 (custodian), F.18 (other property), F.20 (robbery)

sub: Crime Coverages > Inside the Premises - Robbery or Safe Burglary of Other Property
q: Which act is a safe burglary as defined in the 2015 ISO Commercial Crime Coverage Form?
choices: Removing the entire safe from inside the premises
Taking property from a safe that was left unlocked
Opening a locked safe with the correct combination and leaving no marks
Prying open a locked cash drawer at a checkout counter
explain: Safe burglary is the unlawful taking of property from within a locked safe or vault by a person unlawfully entering it, as shown by marks of forcible entry on its exterior, or the taking of a safe or vault itself from inside the premises.

q: A store owner sends an employee to the bank with the day's cash receipts, and the employee loses the bag on the way. Under the 2015 ISO Commercial Crime Coverage Form, which insuring agreement covers the loss?
choices: Employee Theft
Outside the Premises
Inside the Premises – Theft of Money and Securities
Money Orders and Counterfeit Money
explain: Outside the Premises covers money and securities in the care and custody of a messenger or an armored motor vehicle company against theft, disappearance or destruction. A messenger includes an employee who has care and custody of property outside the premises.
source: ISO CR 00 21 11 15, A.5.a; F.15 (messenger)

q: In the 2015 ISO Commercial Crime Coverage Form, Outside the Premises covers other property (not money or securities) in a messenger's care against:
choices: Actual or attempted robbery only
Theft, disappearance or destruction
Any direct physical loss not excluded
Theft only while it is in a locked vehicle
explain: For other property in the care and custody of a messenger or an armored motor vehicle company, Outside the Premises covers only actual or attempted robbery. Money and securities outside the premises are covered against theft, disappearance or destruction.

q: Which loss is covered by the computer fraud part of the Computer and Funds Transfer Fraud insuring agreement in the 2015 ISO Commercial Crime Coverage Form?
choices: An employee with authorized access to the insured's computer system enters a false invoice that pays her
A thief uses stolen credit card numbers to buy goods from the insured's website
An outside hacker changes data in the insured's computer system, causing a payment to the hacker
An employee wires money after an email that appears to come from a supplier asks for payment
explain: The computer fraud part covers loss from a fraudulent entry or change of electronic data or computer programs in a computer system the insured owns, leases or operates that causes money, securities or other property to be transferred, paid or delivered, or the insured's account to be debited. It excludes entries by a person with authorized access to the system, credit card transactions, and loss from an employee acting on a fraudulent instruction.

q: A caller posing as a company's owner phones its bank and has it wire $40,000 from the company's account, which accepts telephone transfer instructions. The owner knew nothing about it. Under the 2015 ISO Commercial Crime Coverage Form, which insuring agreement covers the loss?
choices: Employee Theft
Computer and Funds Transfer Fraud
Forgery or Alteration
Inside the Premises – Theft of Money and Securities
explain: The funds transfer fraud part of this insuring agreement covers loss from a fraudulent instruction directing a financial institution to debit the insured's transfer account and transfer money from it. A fraudulent instruction includes a telephone instruction that purports to come from the insured but was issued by someone else without the insured's knowledge or consent.
source: ISO CR 00 21 11 15, A.6.a.(2); F.12.a.(1) (fraudulent instruction); F.24 (transfer account)

q: A dry cleaner wants inland marine coverage on customers' garments in its care so it can pay customers for a covered loss whether or not it is legally liable. Which coverage is designed for this?
choices: Commercial articles coverage
Equipment dealers coverage
Bailees customers coverage
Jewelers block coverage
explain: Bailees customers coverage insures personal property of others in the insured's care, custody or control, such as customers' clothing at a dry cleaner. Bailees buy it so they can pay customers for losses, not merely to insure their own legal liability.
source: ISO IH 00 85 12 20, A.1 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Bailees Customers Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2023)); FC&S 'Bailee's Customers Insurance' (propertycasualty360.com, 2012); IRMI glossary 'bailee coverage' (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13)

q: A carpet cleaner insured under the 2020 ISO Bailees Customers Coverage Form damages a customer's rug during its own cleaning process. The damage is:
choices: Covered in full
Covered only if the insured was negligent
Covered only while the rug is at the insured's premises
Excluded, except for resulting fire or explosion damage
explain: The form excludes loss caused by processing or work upon the property, but it pays for direct loss caused by a resulting fire or explosion. Negligence is not a condition of coverage, and the exclusion is not limited to the insured's premises.
source: ISO IH 00 85 12 20, B.2.g (form text quoted in FC&S 'Bailees Customers Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2023))

q: Which ISO inland marine coverage form is designed to insure cameras and musical instruments used commercially, such as by a professional photographer or a band?
choices: Signs Coverage Form
Valuable Papers and Records Coverage Form
Commercial Articles Coverage Form
Equipment Dealers Coverage Form
explain: The Commercial Articles Coverage Form covers cameras, projection machines, films and related equipment, musical instruments and related equipment, and similar property of others in the insured's care, custody or control. Typical insureds include photography studios, film production companies and professional musicians.
source: ISO CM 00 20 01 13, A.1 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Commercial Articles Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2014))

q: Where is covered property insured under the 2013 ISO Commercial Articles Coverage Form?
choices: Only at the premises described in the Declarations
Only while in transit
Only within the United States, Puerto Rico and Canada
Wherever located
explain: The form's Coverage Territory condition states: "We cover property wherever located." Other ISO inland marine forms, such as the Signs and Jewelers Block forms, limit coverage to the United States (including its territories and possessions), Puerto Rico and Canada.
