source: ISO CM 00 20 01 13, E.1 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Commercial Articles Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2014)); ISO CM 00 28 01 13, Additional Conditions 1 (quoted in FC&S 'Signs Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2015))

sub: IM Coverage Forms > Contractors Equipment Floater
q: A road-building contractor schedules its equipment under the 2013 ISO Contractors Equipment Coverage Form. Which item is covered property?
choices: A bulldozer it owns and uses on job sites
A dump truck licensed for use on public roads
A backhoe it has rented out to another contractor
Tools and clothing owned by its employees
explain: The form covers the insured's contractor's equipment described in the Declarations and similar property of others in its care, custody or control. It excludes vehicles licensed for use on public roads, property the insured loans, leases or rents to others, and employees' tools and clothing.
source: ISO IH 00 68 12 13, A.1-2 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Contractors Equipment Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2018))

sub: IM Coverage Forms > Electronic Data Processing
q: A business wants open perils inland marine coverage on its computer hardware, software and data storage media. Which coverage is designed for this exposure?
choices: Electronic data processing coverage
Valuable papers and records coverage
Accounts receivable coverage
Commercial articles coverage
explain: EDP (computer systems) coverage, such as ISO's Computer Systems Coverage Form, insures computer equipment, data and media against risks of direct physical loss. Valuable papers and records coverage excludes data processing data, programs and the media on which data is recorded.
source: ISO IH 00 75 09 09, A.1 and A.3 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Computer Systems Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2018)); ISO CM 00 67 01 13, Definitions 1 (quoted in FC&S 'Valuable Papers and Records Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2015))

q: Under an unendorsed 2010 ISO Equipment Dealers Coverage Form, which property of a farm equipment dealer is covered?
choices: Pickup trucks held in stock for sale
Tractors and backhoes held in stock for sale
A combine sold on an installment contract and already delivered
The dealer's office furniture and fixtures
explain: The form covers the dealer's stock in trade, consisting principally of mobile agricultural and construction equipment, and similar property of others in its care. It excludes automobiles and motor trucks, property sold on a deferred payment agreement after it leaves the dealer's custody, and furniture and fixtures (which can be added by endorsement).
source: ISO CM 00 22 03 10, A.1-2 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Equipment Dealers Coverage' (propertycasualty360.com, 2013))

q: A heating and air-conditioning contractor buys rooftop units that it will install in a customer's new building. Which inland marine coverage is designed to cover the units being installed?
choices: Installation floater
Bailees customers coverage
Contractors equipment floater
Equipment dealers coverage
explain: An installation floater is inland marine coverage on property, usually equipment, being installed by a contractor; it is a specialized type of builders risk coverage. A contractors equipment floater covers the contractor's own machinery and tools, not property it is installing.
source: IRMI glossary 'installation floater' (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13); ISO IH 00 68 12 13, A.1 (quoted in FC&S 'Contractors Equipment Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2018))

q: A retail jewelry store wants open perils coverage on its stock of jewelry and watches and on customers' jewelry left for repair. Which coverage is designed for this?
choices: Jewelers block coverage
Bailees customers coverage
Commercial articles coverage
Valuable papers and records coverage
explain: The Jewelers Block Coverage Form covers a jeweler's stock in trade, property sold but not yet delivered, and similar property of others in its care, custody or control, on an open perils basis. The Bailees Customers Coverage Form excludes jewelry, watches and precious stones.
source: ISO CM 00 59 01 13, A.1 and A.3 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Jewelers Block Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2014)); ISO IH 00 85 12 20, A.2.f (quoted in FC&S 'Bailees Customers Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2023))

q: Under the 2013 ISO Jewelers Block Coverage Form, a necklace from the jeweler's stock is NOT covered while it is:
choices: Being worn by one of the insured's employees
Locked in a safe at the insured's premises
Sold but not yet delivered to the buyer
Shipped by U.S. Postal Service registered mail
explain: Property is not covered while being worn by the insured or by an officer, employee or other person in the jewelry trade (watches worn solely for adjustment are an exception). Stock sold but not delivered is covered, and mail shipments are covered if sent by registered mail.
source: ISO CM 00 59 01 13, A.1.b, A.2.d-e (form text quoted in FC&S 'Jewelers Block Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2014))

q: According to ISO's rules for the 2013 Signs Coverage Form, the form may be used to insure:
choices: Billboards along a highway that are lit by floodlights
Neon, fluorescent, automatic or mechanical electric signs
Ordinary fixed signs lit directly by electric lights
Painted wooden signs hung on the insured's storefront
explain: ISO's Commercial Lines Manual limits the Signs Coverage Form to neon, fluorescent, automatic or mechanical electric signs and lamps. Billboards and ordinary fixed signs are ineligible, whether or not they are lit by electric lights.
source: FC&S 'Signs Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2015), describing ISO Commercial Lines Manual rules for CM 00 28 01 13

q: A store insures its neon sign under the 2013 ISO Signs Coverage Form. Which loss is excluded?
choices: A windstorm blows the sign off the building
Vandals break the sign with rocks
A delivery truck backs into the sign
The sign breaks while it is being repaired
explain: The form excludes breakage during transportation, installation, repairing or dismantling, except breakage caused directly by fire, lightning or an accident to the vehicle carrying the property. Windstorm, vandalism and vehicle damage are covered because the form covers direct physical loss except for listed exclusions.
source: ISO CM 00 28 01 13, A.3 and B.2.b (form text quoted in FC&S 'Signs Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2015))

sub: IM Coverage Forms > Valuable Papers and Records
q: Which of the following meets the definition of "valuable papers and records" in the 2013 ISO Valuable Papers and Records Coverage Form?
choices: Cash in the office safe
An architect's original drawings
Customer data stored on a computer server
Stock certificates
explain: "Valuable papers and records" means inscribed, printed or written documents, manuscripts or records, including drawings, maps, deeds and mortgages. The definition excludes money, securities, and data processing data, programs and the media on which the data is recorded.
source: ISO CM 00 67 01 13, Definitions 1 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Valuable Papers and Records Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2015))

sub: IM Coverage Forms > Valuable Papers and Records
q: Under the 2013 ISO Valuable Papers and Records Coverage Form, an irreplaceable original manuscript is covered property only if it is:
choices: Included in the blanket limit for property at the premises
Held by the insured as a sample for a later sale
Kept in storage at a location away from the insured's premises
Specifically declared and described in the Declarations
explain: Property that cannot be replaced with other property of like kind and quality is not covered unless it is specifically declared and described in the Declarations. Property held as samples or for delivery after sale, and property in storage away from the described premises, are not covered.
source: ISO CM 00 67 01 13, A.2.a-c (form text quoted in FC&S 'Valuable Papers and Records Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2015))

sub: Transportation Coverages > Motor Truck Cargo Forms
q: A trucking company hauls other businesses' goods as a common carrier. Which coverage protects the trucker against its legal liability for loss of that cargo?
choices: Annual transit coverage
Motor truck cargo owners coverage
Trip transit coverage
Motor truck cargo carriers coverage
explain: Motor truck cargo carriers coverage is legal liability coverage for a common or contract carrier shipping property of others. Owners coverage and annual or trip transit coverage are first-party coverages on the insured's own property.
source: Verisk, 'Transportation risks are changing' commercial inland marine program sheet (VKUS22142, 2022); FC&S 'Motor Truck Cargo - AAIS' (propertycasualty360.com, 2015)

sub: Transportation Coverages > Motor Truck Cargo Forms
q: A furniture maker ships its own products to customers only on its own trucks. Which coverage is designed to insure the furniture while it is on those trucks?
choices: Motor truck cargo owners coverage
Bailees customers coverage
Contingent cargo coverage for brokers
Motor truck cargo carriers coverage
explain: Motor truck cargo owners coverage is first-party coverage for a business's own property shipped on its own vehicles. Carriers coverage insures a trucker's legal liability for others' cargo, and contingent cargo coverage is for transportation brokers.
source: Verisk, 'Transportation risks are changing' commercial inland marine program sheet (VKUS22142, 2022)

q: A manufacturer wants one policy covering all of its outgoing shipments during the year, whether sent by carriers for hire or on its own trucks. Which coverage fits?
choices: Annual transit coverage
Contingent cargo coverage
Motor truck cargo carriers coverage
Trip transit coverage
explain: Annual transit coverage is first-party coverage for property a business ships by carriers for hire or on its own vehicles during the policy term. Trip transit coverage applies to a single shipment.
source: Verisk, 'Transportation risks are changing' commercial inland marine program sheet (VKUS22142, 2022); IRMI glossary 'trip transit insurance' (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13)

q: Trip transit insurance is written to cover:
choices: All of the insured's shipments during the policy term
A broker's contingent interest in cargo it arranges to ship
A carrier's legal liability for cargo of others
A single, specific shipment
explain: Trip transit insurance covers a specific individual shipment, as distinguished from transit insurance that covers all shipments during the policy term.
source: IRMI glossary 'trip transit insurance' (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13); Verisk, 'Transportation risks are changing' commercial inland marine program sheet (VKUS22142, 2022)

q: Under the ISO farm property forms, which of the following is covered under Coverage A – Dwellings?
choices: A detached garage separated from the dwelling by clear space
A barn used to house dairy cattle
Lumber on the insured location for repairing the covered dwelling
The land on which the dwelling stands
explain: Coverage A covers each dwelling with a limit shown, structures attached to it, and materials on the insured location for building, altering or repairing it. A detached garage falls under Coverage B, a barn under Coverage G, and land is not covered.
source: ISO FP 00 12 04 16, Cov. A, A.1-2 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Personal Exposures FP 00 12' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016)); ISO FP 00 10 09 94, Cov. A 1-2

q: Under the 2016 ISO farm dwelling coverage form, a loss to a farm dwelling is settled at replacement cost if the Coverage A limit is at least what percentage of the dwelling's full replacement cost at the time of loss?
explain: If the limit is at least 80% of full replacement cost, the loss is settled at replacement cost (the smallest of the cost to replace, the amount actually spent, or the limit). Below 80%, the insurer pays the larger of actual cash value or a proportion of the replacement cost.
source: ISO FP 00 12 04 16, Cov. A, B.1.b-c (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Personal Exposures FP 00 12' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016)); same 80% rule in ISO FP 00 10 09 94, Cov. A 7.a(2)-(3)

sub: Farm Property > Coverage B - Other Private Structures
q: A farmer's machine shed is used principally for farming. Under the ISO farm property forms, the shed is insured under:
choices: Coverage G – Other Farm Structures
Coverage A – Dwellings
Coverage B – Other Private Structures
Coverage C – Household Personal Property
explain: Coverage B excludes structures, other than private garages, used principally for farming purposes. Farm buildings and structures other than dwellings are insured under Coverage G when a limit is shown in the Declarations.
source: ISO FP 00 12 04 16, Cov. B, A.2.d (quoted in FC&S 'Farm Personal Exposures FP 00 12' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016)); ISO FP 00 14 04 16, A.1.a (quoted in FC&S 'Farm Property-Barns, Outbuildings, and Other Farm Structures Coverage Form, FP 00 14' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016)); ISO FP 00 10 09 94, Cov. B 2.d and Cov. G 1.a

sub: Farm Property > Coverage B - Other Private Structures
q: How much insurance does Coverage B – Other Private Structures provide under the 2016 ISO farm dwelling coverage form?
choices: 5% of the Coverage A limit, as part of that limit
10% of the Coverage A limit, as part of that limit
10% of the Coverage A limit, as additional insurance
20% of the Coverage A limit, as additional insurance
explain: The most paid in any one occurrence is 10% of the Coverage A limit, and this 10% is additional insurance that does not reduce Coverage A. The 1994 Farm Property Coverage Form applied the automatic 10% only to private garages; other structures needed their own limit.
source: ISO FP 00 12 04 16, Cov. B, A.3.a (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Personal Exposures FP 00 12' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016)); ISO FP 00 10 09 94, Cov. B 1.a-b

sub: Farm Property > Coverage C - Household Personal Property
q: Under the ISO farm property forms, which item is covered under Coverage C – Household Personal Property?
choices: Hay stored in the barn
A herd of beef cattle
Furniture in the farm dwelling
A farm tractor
explain: Coverage C covers household personal property owned or used by the insured and resident family members. It excludes animals and farm personal property (other than office furniture, fixtures and equipment), which are insured under the farm personal property coverages.
source: ISO FP 00 12 04 16, Cov. C, A.1-2 (quoted in FC&S 'Farm Personal Exposures FP 00 12' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016)); ISO FP 00 10 09 94, Cov. C 1-2

sub: Farm Property > Coverage D - Loss of Use
q: Coverage D – Loss of Use under the ISO farm dwelling coverage form pays all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: Income lost when hail destroys the farmer's crops
Additional living expense while the dwelling is uninhabitable
Fair rental value of part of the dwelling rented to others
Loss when a civil authority bars use of the dwelling after covered damage next door
explain: Coverage D pays additional living expense, the fair rental value of a part of the dwelling rented to others, and loss when a civil authority prohibits use because of direct damage to neighboring premises by a covered cause of loss. It does not pay farm business income such as lost crop income.
source: ISO FP 00 12 04 16, Cov. D, A.1-3 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Personal Exposures FP 00 12' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016)); ISO FP 00 10 09 94, Cov. D 1.a-c

sub: Farm Property > Coverage D - Loss of Use
q: When a civil authority prohibits use of a farm dwelling because of covered damage to neighboring premises, the 2016 ISO farm dwelling coverage form pays Coverage D loss incurred during a period of up to:
choices: 1 week
2 weeks
3 weeks
4 weeks
explain: The 2016 edition pays this emergency prohibition-of-occupancy loss for up to three weeks; the 1994 Farm Property Coverage Form allowed 2 weeks. No deductible applies to Coverage D.
source: ISO FP 00 12 04 16, Cov. D, A.3 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Personal Exposures FP 00 12' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016)); ISO FP 00 10 09 94, Cov. D 1.c

sub: Farm Property > Coverage F - Unscheduled Farm Personal Property
q: Which item located on the insured location is covered under Coverage F – Unscheduled Farm Personal Property?
choices: Laying hens
Field fences
A pickup truck licensed for road use
Hay stored in a barn
explain: Coverage F covers all farm personal property on the insured location except property it lists as not covered. Poultry, fences, and vehicles designed and licensed for road use are on that list.
source: ISO FP 00 13 04 16, Cov. F, A.1-2 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Property - Farm Personal Property Coverage Form FP 00 13, Coverages E and F' (propertycasualty360.com, 2017)); ISO FP 00 10 09 94, Cov. F 1-2

sub: Farm Property > Coverage G - Other Farm Structures
q: When a limit is shown for each type of property, Coverage G – Other Farm Structures covers all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: Silos described in the Declarations
Corrals, pens and chutes
Field and pasture fences
Portable buildings
explain: Coverage G covers farm buildings and structures other than dwellings, described silos, portable buildings, and fences, corrals, pens, chutes and feed racks. Field and pasture fences are expressly not covered.
source: ISO FP 00 14 04 16, A.1-2 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Property-Barns, Outbuildings, and Other Farm Structures Coverage Form, FP 00 14' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016)); ISO FP 00 10 09 94, Cov. G 1-2

sub: Farm Property > Coverage G - Other Farm Structures
q: Unless the Declarations indicate the Replacement Cost Basis option, a covered loss to a barn under Coverage G – Other Farm Structures is settled at:
choices: Actual cash value
Agreed value
Market value
Replacement cost
explain: Coverage G property other than improvements and betterments is settled at actual cash value unless the Replacement Cost Basis option is expressly indicated in the Declarations. If it is, the same 80% replacement cost rule used for dwellings applies.
source: ISO FP 00 14 04 16, B.3.a-b (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Property-Barns, Outbuildings, and Other Farm Structures Coverage Form, FP 00 14' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016)); ISO FP 00 10 09 94, Cov. G 6.c

sub: Farm > Mobile Agricultural Machinery and Equipment Form
q: Which ISO farm coverage form is an inland marine form designed for tractors, balers and other mobile devices used in the everyday operation of a farm?
choices: Barns, Outbuildings and Other Farm Structures Coverage Form
Equipment Dealers Coverage Form
Livestock Coverage Form
Mobile Agricultural Machinery and Equipment Coverage Form
explain: The Mobile Agricultural Machinery and Equipment Coverage Form is one of ISO's two farm inland marine forms (the other is the Livestock Coverage Form). It covers mobile devices used in the everyday operation of the farm, including accessories and tools and spare parts designed for them; the Equipment Dealers form is for dealers' stock.
source: FC&S 'Farm Coverage Program' (propertycasualty360.com, 2017) (FP 00 30 04 16); ISO FP 00 30 01 98, A.1 and Definitions (form text quoted in FC&S 'Mobile Agricultural Machinery and Equipment' archive (propertycasualty360.com, 2012))

q: A tenant farmer owns no farm buildings but wants coverage on his cattle and horses. Which ISO form can insure them on a stand-alone basis?
choices: Barns, Outbuildings and Other Farm Structures Coverage Form
Livestock Coverage Form
Mobile Agricultural Machinery and Equipment Coverage Form
Farm Dwellings, Appurtenant Structures and Household Personal Property Coverage Form
explain: The Livestock Coverage Form is an inland marine form that insures livestock on a named perils basis and is available on a stand-alone (monoline) basis, which suits a tenant farmer with no farm buildings. Household personal property coverage excludes animals.
source: IRMI glossary 'livestock coverage form' (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13); ISO FP 00 40 02 09 (quoted in FC&S 'Livestock Coverage' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016)); ISO FP 00 12 04 16, Cov. C, A.2 (quoted in FC&S 'Farm Personal Exposures FP 00 12' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016))

q: Under the ISO Livestock Coverage Form, a covered "loss" of livestock means:
choices: Any injury or illness of the animal
A drop in market value caused by a covered peril
Death from any cause, including disease
Death or destruction of the animal
explain: The form defines "loss" as the death or destruction of livestock, and it covers only named perils such as fire, windstorm, theft, collision, earthquake and flood. It is not a mortality policy covering death from any cause.
source: IRMI glossary 'livestock coverage form' (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13); ISO FP 00 40 02 09, A and A.3 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Livestock Coverage' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016))

q: As defined in the ISO farm property forms, "livestock" includes all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: Goats
Mules
Poultry
Swine
explain: "Livestock" means cattle, sheep, swine, goats, horses, mules and donkeys. "Poultry" (fowl kept for use or sale) is a separately defined term.
source: ISO FP 00 10 09 94, H.6 and H.9; ISO FP 00 40 02 09 (quoted in FC&S 'Livestock Coverage' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016)); IRMI glossary 'livestock coverage form' (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13)

q: Under the ISO farm property forms, which building meets the definition of a "dwelling"?
choices: A barn used to house the farm's livestock
A building used to store the farm's produce
A poultry house used for laying hens
A mobile home used as the family's residence
explain: "Dwelling" means a building used principally for family residential purposes, including mobile, modular and prefabricated homes. It does not include a building used in agricultural operations such as storing produce, livestock or poultry.
source: ISO FP 00 10 09 94, H.2; FC&S 'Farm Personal Exposures FP 00 12' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016) (describing the FP 00 90 04 16 definition)

sub: Farm > Causes of Loss (Basic, Broad, Special)
q: Which peril is included in the Broad causes of loss of the ISO farm property program but not in the Basic causes of loss?
choices: Flood loss to livestock
Riot or civil commotion
Weight of ice, snow or sleet
Windstorm or hail
explain: Broad adds perils such as breakage of glass, falling objects, weight of ice, snow or sleet, water discharge and certain livestock perils to the Basic list. Windstorm or hail, riot or civil commotion, and flood loss to livestock are already Basic perils.
source: ISO FP 10 60 09 03, B-C (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Property Covered Causes of Loss' (propertycasualty360.com, 2012)); FC&S 'Farm Coverage Program' (propertycasualty360.com, 2017) (FP 10 60 04 16); ISO FP 00 10 09 94, B.1-2

sub: Farm > Causes of Loss (Basic, Broad, Special)
q: Under the 2016 ISO Farm Personal Property Coverage Form, livestock insured under Coverage F – Unscheduled Farm Personal Property may be covered for which causes of loss?
choices: Basic causes of loss only
Basic or Broad causes of loss only
Broad or Special causes of loss only
Basic, Broad or Special causes of loss
explain: For livestock, the Basic or Broad causes of loss are the only covered causes of loss. The Special causes of loss cannot be used for livestock or other animals.
source: ISO FP 00 13 04 16, Cov. F, A.1.a (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Property - Farm Personal Property Coverage Form FP 00 13, Coverages E and F' (propertycasualty360.com, 2017)); FC&S 'Farm Property Covered Causes of Loss' (propertycasualty360.com, 2012) (FP 10 60 09 03)

sub: Farm > Causes of Loss (Basic, Broad, Special)
q: Under the Broad causes of loss in the 2003 ISO Causes of Loss Form – Farm Property, which livestock loss is covered?
choices: A cow killed by a neighbor's dogs
Sheep killed by a neighbor's dogs
A hog killed by the insured's own dog
A piglet under 30 days old that drowns
explain: Broad adds attacks on livestock by dogs or wild animals, but not loss to sheep or loss caused by animals owned by the insured, its employees or others living on the insured location. Drowning is also a Broad peril, except for swine under 30 days old.
source: ISO FP 10 60 09 03, C.16 and C.18 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Property Covered Causes of Loss' (propertycasualty360.com, 2012)); same in ISO FP 00 10 09 94, B.2.p and B.2.r

q: Under an unendorsed ISO farm dwelling coverage form, a covered loss to household personal property under Coverage C is settled at:
choices: Agreed value
Actual cash value
Replacement cost
Stated amount
explain: The Coverage C Loss Condition – Valuation settles household personal property at actual cash value at the time of loss, but not more than the amount needed to repair or replace it. Replacement cost on household personal property requires an endorsement.
source: ISO FP 00 12 04 16, Cov. C Loss Condition – Valuation (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Personal Exposures FP 00 12' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016)); ISO FP 00 10 09 94, Cov. C 7; FC&S listing 'FP 04 36 04 16 Replacement Cost - Household Personal Property' (propertycasualty360.com, 2024)

q: To avoid a coinsurance penalty under the 2016 ISO Farm Personal Property Coverage Form, unscheduled farm personal property (Coverage F) must be insured for at least what percentage of its actual cash value?
explain: Coverage F's Coinsurance loss condition requires insurance of at least 80% of actual cash value at the time of loss. Otherwise the insurer pays the proportion that the limit carried bears to the limit required.
source: ISO FP 00 13 04 16, Cov. F, B.2 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Property - Farm Personal Property Coverage Form FP 00 13, Coverages E and F' (propertycasualty360.com, 2017)); same 80% in ISO FP 00 10 09 94, Cov. F 7.b

q: The ISO farm causes of loss exclude flood, but flood loss is covered for:
choices: Barns and other farm structures
Farm dwellings
Livestock
Household personal property
explain: The Water exclusion does not apply to flood loss to livestock or to farm machinery covered for the Special causes of loss, and the Basic causes of loss list flood loss to livestock as a covered peril. Buildings and household goods remain subject to the flood exclusion.
source: ISO FP 10 60 09 03, B.14 and E.9 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Property Covered Causes of Loss' (propertycasualty360.com, 2012)); ISO FP 00 10 09 94, B.1.n and C.8; ISO FP 00 40 02 09, A.3.m (quoted in FC&S 'Livestock Coverage' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016))

q: Fire destroys a barn insured under an unendorsed ISO farm property policy, and a local ordinance requires the new barn to meet a stricter building code. The extra cost to comply with the ordinance is:
choices: Covered under the Basic causes of loss
Not covered
Covered only under the Broad or Special causes of loss
Covered only if the barn is insured for replacement cost
explain: The farm causes of loss exclude loss from enforcement of any ordinance or law regulating construction or repair, at every level (Basic, Broad and Special). The Coverage G valuation condition also states that repair or replacement cost does not include costs to comply with such ordinances. Ordinance or law coverage for farm buildings other than dwellings is available by endorsement.
source: ISO FP 10 60 09 03, E.1 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Property Covered Causes of Loss' (propertycasualty360.com, 2012)); ISO FP 00 14 04 16, B.3 (quoted in FC&S 'Farm Property-Barns, Outbuildings, and Other Farm Structures Coverage Form, FP 00 14' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016)); ISO FP 00 10 09 94, C.1; FC&S 'Farm Property Endorsements Discussed' (propertycasualty360.com, 2024) (FP 04 05 Ordinance or Law Coverage)

q: In the 2016 ISO farm dwelling coverage form, the special limit for money under Coverage C – Household Personal Property is:
explain: Coverage C has a $200 special limit on money, gold other than goldware, platinum other than platinumware, and silver other than silverware. Special limits are part of, not in addition to, the Coverage C limit.
source: ISO FP 00 12 04 16, Cov. C, A.3.a (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Personal Exposures FP 00 12' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016)); ISO FP 00 10 09 94, Cov. C 3.a

q: A 4-year-old dairy cow insured under Coverage F – Unscheduled Farm Personal Property is killed by lightning. Under the 2016 ISO Farm Personal Property Coverage Form, the most Coverage F pays for this one animal is:
explain: Coverage F's special limits are $1,000 on any horse, mule or head of cattle under one year old and $2,000 on any other head of livestock. A 4-year-old cow falls in the $2,000 class; the limits are part of the Coverage F limit.
source: ISO FP 00 13 04 16, Cov. F, A.3 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Property - Farm Personal Property Coverage Form FP 00 13, Coverages E and F' (propertycasualty360.com, 2017)); ISO FP 00 10 09 94, Cov. F 3

q: The 2016 ISO farm dwelling coverage form's additional coverage for credit card, fund transfer card, forgery and counterfeit currency losses pays up to how much, unless a higher limit is shown in the Declarations?
explain: This additional coverage pays up to $500 unless a higher limit is indicated in the Declarations. The 1994 Farm Property Coverage Form also provided $500.
source: ISO FP 00 12 04 16, Sec. III, B.1 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Personal Exposures FP 00 12' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016)); ISO FP 00 10 09 94, D.2.b(1)

q: The Removal of Fallen Trees additional coverage in the 2016 ISO farm dwelling coverage form pays at most:
choices: $500 per loss
$500 per tree, up to $1,000 per loss
$1,000 per tree, up to $2,500 per loss
$1,000 per tree, up to $5,000 per loss
explain: The 2016 form pays up to $1,000 in any one loss for removing fallen trees, with no more than $500 for any one tree, as additional insurance. The 1994 Farm Property Coverage Form paid no more than $500 in total.
source: ISO FP 00 12 04 16, Sec. III, A.3 (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Personal Exposures FP 00 12' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016)); ISO FP 00 10 09 94, D.2.a

sub: Farm Liability > Coverage H - BI and PD Liability
q: A farmer's cattle break through a fence and trample a neighbor's crops. The neighbor sues the farmer for the damage. Which farm coverage responds?
choices: Coverage F – Unscheduled Farm Personal Property
Coverage H – Bodily Injury and Property Damage Liability
Coverage I – Personal and Advertising Injury Liability
Coverage J – Medical Payments
explain: Coverage H pays sums the insured is legally obligated to pay as damages because of bodily injury or property damage caused by an occurrence, and the insurer defends the suit. Coverage J pays only medical expenses for bodily injury, Coverage I applies to personal and advertising injury offenses, and Coverage F insures the farmer's own property.
source: ISO FL 00 20 10 06, Sec. I, Cov. H 1.a, Cov. I 1.a, Cov. J 1.a (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Liability Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2013)); ISO FP 00 13 04 16, Cov. F (quoted in FC&S 'Farm Property - Farm Personal Property Coverage Form FP 00 13, Coverages E and F' (propertycasualty360.com, 2017))

sub: Farm Liability > Coverage H - BI and PD Liability
q: Under the 2006 ISO Farm Liability Coverage Form, Coverage H applies to bodily injury or property damage that:
choices: Is first claimed during the policy period, whenever it occurred
Is caused by an offense committed during the policy period
Is reported to the insurer within 3 years after the accident
Occurs during the policy period and is caused by an occurrence
explain: Coverage H is occurrence-based: the bodily injury or property damage must be caused by an occurrence and must occur during the policy period. The offense trigger belongs to Coverage I, and the 3-year period relates to Coverage J medical expenses.
source: ISO FL 00 20 10 06, Cov. H 1.b, Cov. I 1.b, Cov. J 1.a (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Liability Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2013))

sub: Farm Liability > Coverage I - Personal and Advertising Injury
q: A neighbor sues a farmer for slander. Which coverage of the Farm Liability Coverage Form is designed to respond?
choices: Coverage H – Bodily Injury and Property Damage Liability
Coverage J – Medical Payments
Damage to Property of Others additional coverage
Coverage I – Personal and Advertising Injury Liability
explain: Coverage I pays damages because of "personal injury" or "advertising injury." Personal injury includes oral or written publication of material that slanders or libels a person or organization, as well as false arrest, malicious prosecution, wrongful eviction and invasion of privacy.
source: ISO FL 00 20 10 06, Cov. I 1.a and Sec. IV definition of "personal injury" (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Liability Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2013))

sub: Farm Liability > Coverage I - Personal and Advertising Injury
q: Under the 2006 ISO Farm Liability Coverage Form, Coverage I applies to personal injury caused by an offense that:
choices: Is committed during the policy period
Is first reported during the policy period
Arises out of civic or public activities performed for pay
Is committed knowing it violates another's rights
explain: Personal injury is covered only if caused by an offense committed during the policy period and arising out of personal activities or operations usual or incidental to farming. Offenses arising out of civic or public activities the insured performs for pay, or committed with knowledge that the act would violate another's rights, are excluded. Coverage I is not claims-made, so the date of first report is not the trigger.
source: ISO FL 00 20 10 06, Cov. I 1.b, 2.a(1) and 2.b(2) (form text quoted in FC&S 'Farm Liability Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2013))

q: Errors and omissions insurance is generally designed to cover the insured's liability for:
choices: Bodily injury to customers on the insured's premises
Damage to customers' property in the insured's care
Financial loss to clients caused by professional mistakes
Theft of the insured's money or securities by its employees
explain: E&O insurance protects the insured against liability for an error or omission in performing professional duties. It is generally designed to cover financial losses rather than bodily injury or property damage.
source: IRMI glossary: errors and omissions insurance (E&O) (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13)

q: A producer forgets to add a client's newly bought warehouse to the client's property policy. The warehouse burns, and the client sues the producer for the uninsured loss. Which coverage is designed for this claim?
choices: Commercial general liability
Errors and omissions
Directors and officers liability
Employment practices liability
explain: The claim alleges a mistake in the producer's professional duties that caused the client a financial loss, which is what E&O insurance covers. A CGL policy covers bodily injury, property damage, and personal and advertising injury, not a client's financial loss from a professional mistake; D&O covers directors and officers for wrongful acts in those roles; EPLI covers employment-related claims such as wrongful termination.
source: IRMI glossary: errors and omissions insurance (E&O); professional liability; employment practices liability insurance (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13); ISO Commercial General Liability Coverage Form CG 00 01 04 13, Sec. I, Coverage A, 1.a

q: Most professional liability policies are written on which coverage trigger?
choices: Occurrence basis
Accident basis
Loss-sustained basis
Claims-made basis
explain: IRMI notes that the vast majority of professional liability policies use a claims-made trigger. A claims-made policy is triggered when a claim is made against the insured during the policy period, regardless of when the wrongful act took place.
source: IRMI glossary: professional liability; claims-made policy; lawyers professional liability coverage (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13)

q: Under most professional liability policies, the insurer's payment of defense costs:
choices: Reduces the limit of insurance available for damages
Is paid in addition to the limit of insurance
Is covered only if the insured wins the suit
Is split equally between the insurer and the insured
explain: Most professional liability policies use a defense-within-limits (shrinking limits) provision: defense costs reduce the available limit. In a CGL policy, defense costs are supplementary payments that do not reduce the limits.
source: IRMI glossary: professional liability; defense within limits; shrinking limits defense provision (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13); ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Supplementary Payments - Coverages A and B

q: A professional liability policy provision that requires the insurer to get the insured's approval before settling a claim is called a(n):
choices: Assistance and cooperation clause
Other insurance clause
Consent to settlement clause
Subrogation clause
explain: The consent to settlement clause, also called the hammer clause, requires the insurer to seek the insured's approval before settling a claim for a specific amount. If the insured rejects the recommended settlement, the insurer is not liable for any additional amount needed to settle or for defense costs that accrue after its recommendation.
source: IRMI glossary: consent to settlement clause (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13)

q: A surgeon makes an error during an operation, and the patient is injured and sues the surgeon. Which coverage is designed for this claim?
choices: Commercial general liability insurance
Directors and officers liability insurance
Workers' compensation insurance
Medical malpractice insurance
explain: Medical malpractice insurance, a form of professional liability, covers the acts, errors and omissions of physicians and surgeons. Physicians are an exception to the rule that professional liability covers only financial loss, and CGL policies are commonly endorsed to exclude professional services such as medical care.
source: IRMI glossary: medical malpractice insurance; professional liability; professional services exclusion (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13)

sub: Surety Bonds > License and Permit Bonds
q: A city will not issue a business license until the applicant posts a bond guaranteeing that it will comply with the city's ordinances. This bond is a:
choices: Bid bond
Probate fiduciary bond
Construction performance bond
License and permit bond
explain: A license and permit bond is required by a municipality or other public body as a condition of granting a license or permit, and guarantees that the licensee will comply with applicable laws or regulations. Bid and performance bonds guarantee a contractor's obligations on a construction contract; a fiduciary bond guarantees a court-appointed fiduciary's faithful performance.
source: IRMI glossary: license and permit bond; fiduciary bond; surety bond (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13); FC&S, "License and Permit Bonds" (Feb. 2010, propertycasualty360.com)

sub: Surety Bonds > License and Permit Bonds
q: On a license and permit bond, the obligee is the:
choices: Government body that issues the license
Business that applies for the license
Surety company that issues the bond
Producer who arranges the bond for the applicant
explain: A license and permit bond guarantees to the governmental unit that requires it (the obligee) that the licensee (the principal) will comply with the regulations that apply to its activity. The surety is the party that gives the guarantee.
source: FC&S, "License and Permit Bonds" (Feb. 2010, propertycasualty360.com); IRMI glossary: license and permit bond; surety bond (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13)

q: Judicial bonds fall into which two general classes?
choices: Bid bonds and payment bonds
Fiduciary bonds and litigation bonds
License bonds and permit bonds
Performance bonds and maintenance bonds
explain: Judicial bonds consist of two classes: fiduciary bonds, which guarantee that persons the court entrusts with others' property perform faithfully and account for it, and court (litigation) bonds, which guarantee payment of damages or costs if the bonded party's court action fails. Bid, performance and payment bonds guarantee a contractor's obligations on a construction contract.
source: FC&S, "Judicial Bonds" (Aug. 2000, propertycasualty360.com); IRMI glossary: surety bond (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13); FAR 48 CFR 28.001

q: A defendant loses a lawsuit and wants to appeal to a higher court. Which bond guarantees payment of the judgment, interest and court costs if the higher court rules against the defendant?
choices: Appeal bond
Attachment bond
Bail bond
Fiduciary bond
explain: An appeal bond posted by the losing party guarantees payment of the entire judgment plus interest and court costs if the higher court rules against it. An attachment bond protects a defendant whose property a plaintiff has attached; a bail bond guarantees that a criminal defendant appears in court.
source: FC&S, "Judicial Bonds" (Aug. 2000, propertycasualty360.com), Appeal Bonds; Attachment Bonds; Bail Bonds

q: Under Michigan's Estates and Protected Individuals Code, a bond that a court requires of a conservator is conditioned upon the conservator's:
choices: Appearance at each scheduled court hearing
Compliance with all local business licensing ordinances
Faithful discharge of all duties of the trust
Payment of personal debts owed to creditors
explain: A conservator's bond is conditioned upon faithful discharge of all duties of the conservator's trust according to law, with sureties as the court specifies. It is a fiduciary bond, one of the two classes of judicial bonds.
source: MCL 700.5410(2) (EPIC); FC&S, "Judicial Bonds" (Aug. 2000, propertycasualty360.com)

q: Under a boatowners policy, which coverage pays the damages an insured is legally entitled to recover from the owner or operator of an uninsured boat because of the insured's bodily injury?
choices: Medical payments
Personal liability
Physical damage
Uninsured boaters
explain: Uninsured boaters coverage pays the compensatory damages an insured is legally entitled to recover from the owner or operator of an uninsured boat because of the insured's bodily injury. Personal liability pays sums the insured is legally liable to pay others; medical payments pays necessary medical expenses; physical damage covers the boat itself.
source: AAIS Boatowners Policy BT 0100, Coverage Z - Uninsured Boaters, as quoted in FC&S, "AAIS Boatowners Program" (July 2008, propertycasualty360.com); IRMI glossary: boatowners policy (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13)

q: Ann has an HO-3 policy and buys a $25,000 fishing boat with an outboard motor. Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms, which provision is the main reason she needs a boatowners policy to insure the boat for its value?
choices: Coverage C excludes watercraft and their motors
Coverage C limits watercraft and their motors to $1,500
Coverage C covers watercraft and their motors only for theft
Coverage A covers watercraft and their motors only on premises
explain: The 2011 HO-3 has a $1,500 special limit on watercraft of all types, including their trailers, furnishings, equipment and outboard engines or motors. It also covers them only for named perils: windstorm or hail loss is covered only while they are inside a fully enclosed building, and theft away from the residence premises is excluded. A boatowners policy fills this property gap.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I, Coverage C Special Limits 3.c; Perils Insured Against (Coverage C) 2 and 9.b.(4)(b); IRMI glossary: boatowners policy (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13)

q: A business's liability policy has a $1,000,000 limit and a $50,000 self-insured retention. A covered claim costs $150,000 in defense and damages. How is the claim paid?
choices: The insurer pays all $150,000 and then bills the insured for $50,000
The insurer pays $100,000, and the claimant absorbs $50,000
The insured pays the first $50,000, and the insurer pays $100,000
The insured pays $150,000 and is later reimbursed $100,000
explain: Under a self-insured retention, the insured itself pays defense and indemnity costs until the retention is reached, and the insurer pays covered amounts after that. Paying the whole claim and then billing the insured is how a deductible works.
source: IRMI glossary: self-insured retention (SIR) (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13)

q: Under Michigan's no-fault law, a business that wants to qualify as a self-insurer for its registered motor vehicles must obtain a certificate of self-insurance from the:
choices: Michigan Catastrophic Claims Association
Workers' Disability Compensation Agency
Director of Insurance and Financial Services
Michigan Automobile Insurance Placement Facility
explain: The certificate is issued by the commissioner, now the DIFS Director, at his or her discretion, if satisfied that the applicant has and will continue to have the ability to pay judgments against it. DIFS rules say the certificate is security equivalent to a no-fault insurance policy; the applicant must also carry excess insurance acceptable to the Director.
source: MCL 500.3101d(1)-(2) (added by 2012 PA 204, eff. January 1, 2013); Mich. Admin. Code R 257.532(1)-(3) (eff. March 15, 2018); DIFS form FIS 2271 (04/25), Application for Self-Insurance Certificate

q: What distinguishes self-insurance from noninsurance?
choices: Self-insurance uses a formal plan to fund and pay losses
Self-insurance transfers the risk to another party
Self-insurance applies only to losses below a deductible
Self-insurance is used only for liability exposures
explain: Self-insurance is a formal decision to retain risk, set aside funds and pay losses from them; a formalized plan or system to pay losses distinguishes it from noninsurance and from retention through deductibles. Under noninsurance, uninsured losses are simply absorbed as a direct expense.
source: IRMI glossary: self-insurance; noninsurance; retention (irmi.com, retrieved 2026-10-13)

q: Under Michigan's no-fault law, a person may qualify as a self-insurer if more than how many motor vehicles are registered in that person's name?
explain: A person in whose name more than 25 motor vehicles are registered may qualify as a self-insurer by obtaining a certificate of self-insurance from the commissioner (DIFS Director). DIFS rules count vehicles registered in Michigan and exclude trailers.
source: MCL 500.3101d(1) (added by 2012 PA 204, eff. January 1, 2013); Mich. Admin. Code R 257.532(2)(a) (eff. March 15, 2018)
